5e Spell Maker: Desktop launcher for a local mirror of a browser tool that formats homebrew D&D 5e spells like sourcebook entries and exports them as images. A preservation mirror of a third-party itch.io tool so it keeps working if the original page goes down, wrapped as a local app. Writing a homebrew spell for a campaign; exporting a spell card image; handing a player a formatted spell.
5eTools: App launcher that starts a local web server on port 5050 for the 5eTools D&D reference site stored in Google Drive and opens it in the browser. Appears to be a one-click way to run the self-hosted 5etools reference offline for D&D prep. Looking up spells, monsters and items during game prep; testing homebrew data locally; opening the reference without terminal steps.
aa-get: Command-line search and download for Anna's Archive. It searches the live mirror in headless Chromium, past the DDoS-Guard check, and downloads a book by its md5 from Libgen first and then the free slow partner servers, resuming each transfer until the size matches. Built to fetch the Spelljammer sourcebooks for The Great Wheel without a membership. Use it whenever a project needs a book, rulebook, magazine scan or paper: to find the md5 of the best copy, or to fetch several files with retries.
actual-gameplay replay + audit: Two Python scripts that drive the Actual Gameplay iPhone app in the simulator: replay.py plays each level's stored solution, audit.py stress-tests levels and prints TRIVIAL, FRAGILE or BROKEN verdicts. Appears to exist so puzzle levels can be regression-tested and difficulty-checked automatically instead of by hand-playing each one after every change. After editing level data or game physics; before shipping a new level; checking whether a level can be solved by sloppy input.
add-reminder: Wrapper around a Swift EventKit helper that creates Apple Reminders with due dates and repeat rules, rebuilding the binary when the source changes. Built because AppleScript cannot set recurrence on Reminders, so repeating reminders needed EventKit. Creating a one-off or repeating Apple Reminder from a script; scheduling a daily or weekly nudge; any reminder needing a due time or recurrence.
aggregator.py (job-search ATS dataset la: Discovery script that filters an open daily dataset of about 1.4 million postings scraped from seven applicant-tracking platforms (Workday, iCIMS, Greenhouse, Paylocity, BambooHR, Ashby, Lever) down to remote-US and Kansas City metro titles first seen in a time window. Built so the job scan reaches employers that are not yet in the tracker, which the per-employer ATS watchlists cannot see. Finding new employers hiring for a title; sweeping every ATS for fresh remote postings; checking which local companies posted IT roles this week.
ai-bill-scan: Python script that scans govinfo BILLSTATUS bulk zips for a whole Congress and emits JSON of every AI-related bill plus a per-member sponsor and cosponsor index with party and date. Built to answer questions like which members of a party have signed AI-risk legislation from primary-source signatures instead of recalled or scraped lists, without an API key or rate limit. Whip counts on AI legislation by party; checking who sponsored or cosponsored a given class of AI bill; refreshing the data after a new Congress zip is published; prepping advocacy or office-outreach research.
alarm-triage: Stdlib Python script summarizing guard-hook denials and notification banners over a time window, grouped by rule and title, with repeat offenders. Built because nothing read back the harness's alarm streams, so recurring false alarms and noisy watchers went unnoticed. Weekly review of harness alarms; finding which rule or watcher to fix; investigating a burst of banners.
alltrails: A command-line tool for AllTrails that searches trails by name, prints trail stats and descriptions, lists recent reviews with their dates and reported conditions, writes the route as a GPX track, and shows the 7-day trailhead forecast. It also uploads GPX files to the user's own account as shareable custom routes, one map segment for each GPX track, and deletes them again. It was built on 2026-10-06 while planning a backpacking trip, because AllTrails blocks plain HTTP requests and its MCP server has no reviews, route geometry or write tools. Use it to compare candidate trails, to check recent conditions such as mud, flooding or ticks, to load a trail route into a GPS app, or to turn a planned multi-day route into a link that a hiking group can open on their phones.
ami-play: Unofficial Python CLI for the AMI Play jukebox app that finds bars, reads live queues and pricing, searches the catalog, and queues songs. Built to control bar jukeboxes from the terminal and let MIST see or queue music without the phone app. Checking what is playing at a bar; searching a song; queueing a track; managing favorites or playlists.
analyze-leaf: Offline analyzer for a WaveLynx LEAF MIFARE DESFire NFC dump that tests whether a candidate master key reproduces the card's free-read CMAC signature. Built as the verification instrument for the challenge of obtaining a LEAF keyset for the apartment fob project, since a candidate key can be checked without the card or reader present. Testing a guessed master key against a fob dump; validating the diversification math with --selftest; confirming a keyset before deriving per-app keys from a UID.
ancestry-dna: A read-only command-line exporter for the user's own AncestryDNA match list. It borrows the logged-in ancestry.com session from Chrome, calls the private JSON endpoints that the match list page uses, and writes CSV files of matches (name, shared cM, segments, predicted relationship, tree flags) and of shared matches, then builds Leeds-method clusters. It was built for an unknown-parent search on a free Ancestry account, because Ancestry has no export, no API and no MCP server, and the older Chrome-extension endpoints now return Access denied. Use it to export DNA matches for analysis, to sort matches into grandparent lines, to find which clusters a known relative touches, or to refresh the data after new matches arrive.
Animal Kill Clock: macOS desktop widget showing a live running count of animals killed for food so far this year, styled after the U.S. Animal Kill Clock website. Built to keep that statistic visible on the desktop as an ambient reminder. Launching the widget after login or a crash; checking the current year-to-date count.
Anna's Archive: Local Flask app in a native window that finds the current working Anna's Archive domain from several feeds, verifies it, and scaffolds member features. Built because the site rotates domains as they get seized, so an always-current entry point saves hunting for the live address. Opening Anna's Archive without knowing the current domain; searching for a book; extending the membership download features.
app-shell build-app: Shell script that builds a native /Applications .app wrapping a localhost web app in a WKWebView window, using a shared Python venv and a launchd kickstart. Built so local web apps get a real Dock icon, menu-bar name and their own TCC identity instead of living in a browser tab. Used by The Priory and Trawl. Turning a new localhost web app into a double-clickable app; rebuilding a wrapper after changing its URL, icon or launchd label; fixing a wrapper's permissions identity.
arctic-shift-scan: Python scanner that pulls every post from a subreddit over the last N days via the Arctic Shift archive API, plus megathread comment trees, into a JSON snapshot. Reddit's unauthenticated JSON endpoints are blocked, so this reads a public archive without Reddit credentials to feed the local events skill with Kansas City posts. Weekly local-events discovery; checking what a city subreddit is discussing; any job needing bulk Reddit post history without an API key.
asc-create-app: Creates an App Store Connect app record by running the website's own request inside a saved signed-in Chrome profile. Built because the App Store Connect API key cannot create apps, which blocked the first TestFlight upload of every new iOS app. Use it when a new app needs its record before bin/testflight-upload, or when a TestFlight upload fails because no app exists for the bundle id.
audio-features: Measures a song for a music video: a fixed beat grid fitted to the tracked beats, downbeats from the beat_this neural tracker when its output is present, kick, snare and hat hits from a Demucs drum stem, and vocal, mix and drum loudness at one value per video frame. It writes JSON plus a script file that a browser page can load. It was built so a kinetic typography video could pump type weight with the voice and move shapes on the beat. Use it to drive any beat-synced animation, to check a song's tempo and bar phase, or to get a per-frame loudness curve.
audiotee: A macOS command-line tool that captures the audio output of chosen processes, or of the whole system, through Apple's Core Audio process taps (macOS 14.2 or later) and writes raw PCM chunks to standard output. It was adopted to feed the govee-music light sync daemon with Pocket Bard's audio without a virtual audio device and without muting the speakers. Use it to analyze what an app is playing in real time, to record one app's audio to a file, to feed a transcription or beat detector from system audio, or to mute one app while sampling it.
auto-update.sh: Shell script that upgrades Homebrew formulae and casks, Mac App Store apps, global npm packages, uv tools and cargo binaries, and records which packages changed major version. It was made after a Node security advisory found Homebrew node two months out of date and more than one hundred formulae stale, because nothing upgraded installed software on a schedule. Use it to bring the whole toolchain current after a security advisory, to find which major upgrade broke a dependent tool, or to check when a package last changed version.
av-sync-check: Checks a rendered music video against its song using only the encoded file. It cross-correlates the MP4's audio track with the source mix to find any sample lag, and finds the frame-difference spikes at the cut times the renderer intended, reporting how many land on the exact frame. It was built to prove a 60 fps lyric video was in sync without watching it. Use it after any render and mux, after re-encoding or trimming a video, or to catch a dropped or shifted frame.
avatar-fit: Python script that fits an image's minimum enclosing circle to a circular avatar crop and verifies that no opaque pixel falls outside it. Built after logos shipped clipped in circular profile croppers such as ESPN Fantasy, where padding to a square was not enough. Preparing a profile picture for a circular cropper; checking whether a logo will clip; setting a background color and size.
bc-rank: Python CLI that reads Bugcrowd's public, logged-out program endpoints (program list, brief scope JSON, statistics, crowdstream of accepted submissions) and writes a ranked CSV and Markdown table. Built to choose which Bugcrowd programs to work first when building a researcher record fast: it measures each vendor's real submit-to-accept time from its own accepted submissions and scores how easy a first valid finding is. Use it to pick a bug bounty target, to compare vendor response speed, to find programs that accept and pay for low-severity bugs, or to re-check the ranking after a few weeks.
Bestagon: Local Flask web app on port 5019 for managing hex-grid combat encounters, loading JSON maps with 5 ft flat-top hexes. Made as a tabletop battle-map manager for Alex's campaigns; the name is a pun on hexagons being the bestagons. Running or prepping a combat encounter on a hex map; adding a new map JSON to the maps folder; testing a hex-grid rule.
bg3save: Reads Baldur's Gate 3 save files (.lsv) on the Mac and prints the game state as JSON: region and act, party members with class, level and XP, story flags, companion approval, quest state, and possibly missed content checked against bg3.wiki. It was set up so MIST can act as an advisor during a BG3 playthrough without screen access, by reading the newest quicksave instead of screenshots. Use it when Alex asks what to do next in BG3, whether he missed a quest, how a companion feels about him, or to diff two saves to see what a choice changed.
bg3wiki-mcp: Gives Claude Code sessions search, page reading and structured Cargo queries against bg3.wiki, the Baldur's Gate 3 community wiki, through ProfessionalWiki's MediaWiki MCP server. Adopted instead of building a wiki scraper when Alex and MIST started playing BG3 split screen. Use it to look up a spell, item, class feature, quest step or character mid-game, or to query the wiki's data tables for builds and loot.
birth-chart-auto: One-command natal chart packet builder in the birth-charts repo. It geocodes a birthplace offline, computes the chart with the Swiss Ephemeris, ranks the chart's signatures, and writes a complete reading from rule tables with no language model, then renders a PDF (or HTML). It was built to replace the hand-written content modules for routine charts and to let anyone run the repo from a pasted GitHub link in Claude Chat. A second layer briefs a writer and checks their prose against the chart so wrong placements cannot reach the page. Use it when someone asks for a birth chart, natal chart or astrology reading, when you need a chart's key signatures fast, or when you need to fact-check astrology prose against real placements.
ble-run: A command-line wrapper that runs Bluetooth LE Python scripts (bleak) inside a small macOS app bundle, /Applications/BLE Run.app, which carries the Bluetooth usage key. It was made because macOS kills bare python with exit 134 when it touches Bluetooth from the MIST Console or a terminal, and the existing Flipper and NIU bundles each run only one fixed script. Its built-in scan mode records every nearby BLE advertiser with signal strength, name, service UUIDs and manufacturer data. Use it to find out if a Bluetooth device is in range and advertising, to get the CoreBluetooth address of a new gadget, to run a one-off bleak probe against a device, or to start reverse-engineering a device's BLE protocol.
bookmarklet-favicon: Gives javascript: bookmarklets a favicon in Chrome, Brave and other Chromium browsers by writing the icon rows into the profile's Favicons SQLite database, keyed by the bookmark's exact URL, which is what the bookmarks bar looks up. It was built because bookmarklets have no host, so browsers never fetch an icon for them and the bar shows a globe; the harness bookmarklets page had been leaning on an emoji in each name instead. Icons come from a manifest (bookmarklets/icons.json), the emoji a bookmark name starts with, or a letter badge, and can be an emoji, a Material Symbol on a rounded square, text, an image file, a site's existing favicon, or a fetched one. Use it after adding or renaming a bookmarklet, when bookmark icons went missing after a profile reset, to preview planned icons as a PNG sheet, or to prove with a headless copy of Chrome (chrome://favicon2) that an icon is served.
Bookmarklets page: Static local HTML page of draggable javascript: bookmarklets, such as Wayback Machine snapshot and Save Page Now, defined in a single BM object. Appears to have been built to keep browser bookmarklets in one version-controlled place instead of hand-made bookmarks. Adding a new bookmarklet; dragging the set into a fresh browser; archiving the current page to the Wayback Machine.
cad: Command-line 3D printing toolkit: builds a part from a build123d Python script, an OpenSCAD file, or a signed-distance-field mesh script, exports STL, STEP and 3MF, runs a printability report (watertight, bodies, bed fit, overhang share, mass), repairs broken meshes with pymeshfix, renders preview sheets and close-ups with f3d, converts mesh formats, slices with PrusaSlicer for print time, filament and stability warnings, and makes Blender studio renders in clay or vertex colour. Built in October 2026 so MIST can design printable parts in code and show them in the Console's inline 3D viewer instead of using a GUI CAD app. Use it to design a bracket, clip, case or holder to measured dimensions; to turn a picture into a printable replica; to check whether a downloaded STL will print; to show Alex a polished render of a part before he prints it.
cad-setup: Installer for the 3D printing toolkit: creates the Python 3.12 venv with build123d, trimesh, manifold3d and pymeshfix, installs OpenSCAD snapshot, PrusaSlicer and f3d through Homebrew, and clones or updates the BOSL2 OpenSCAD library. Exists so the cad CLI can be rebuilt on a fresh machine or after a broken brew upgrade in one step. Use it when cad reports a missing venv, when BOSL2 needs updating, or when setting up the toolkit on another Mac.
card: Script that renders a 1200 by 630 social preview image from a small card page of the Midwest AI data center atlas, using a headless browser. It was made so links to the atlas show the map and title when shared. Use it to refresh the preview image after a data update, or as a pattern for making a link-preview image from any web page.
census.py: A command-line script that counts how much text the principal wrote or said in each local data source, and tags every record as certain, likely, or unknown authorship and by register (chat, spoken, email, prompt, notes, published). It prints a table of items, words, and estimated tokens and writes the counts to a JSON file, without writing any corpus text. It was made as Phase 0 of the guardian-angel research, to measure whether a personal corpus is big enough to finetune a model of the principal. Use it to re-measure the corpus after a new data source is added, to check how much a diarization or Discord backfill adds, or to confirm that an extractor excludes assistant-written text before a training run.
chat-draft: Python CLI managing fantasy league chat reply drafts: save, list, show, send, skip, with a check that refuses to send into a moved-on thread. Built after 2026-09-20 so chat replies are never sent unattended, and a human approves each reply. Saving or reviewing a draft; sending an approved reply; skipping one; overriding the stale-thread check.
chat-watch: Python watcher run every 10 minutes that finds unanswered ESPN Fantasy Chat threads and has a headless Claude decide whether to reply, keyed by message ID. Built to keep league chat answered promptly while ensuring direct messages go to Alex rather than getting an unattended reply. Debugging a missed or double reply; running with --dry-run; adjusting the daily reply cap; checking how direct messages are handed off.
check_boundaries.py: AST-based checker that fails when a script in one top-level harness directory imports another directory's internals or adds a sibling directory to sys.path. Written because the harness is a set of independent hyphenated scripts that import-linter cannot model, and cross-tool coupling needed to be caught automatically after each edit. Runs automatically in the post-edit quality-gate hook; run it by hand across the whole repo before a large refactor; add a blessed cross-island import to its allow list when a deliberate shared interface is needed.
Chromatic Set: Local Flask app on port 5018 that reads every pixel of an uploaded image and turns color into pitch-class sets to compose a roughly two-minute piece. Appears to have been built to explore mapping the hue wheel onto the twelve-tone chromatic circle, using real Forte set theory to read an image as music. Turning a picture into a composition; demonstrating pitch-class set theory; experimenting with color-to-pitch mappings.
cl-404: A Python script in the Common Lot repo that draws the site's 404 banner: a survey-style plat of a real vacant Land Bank lot, with neighboring parcel lines from the Kansas City GIS and house outlines from OpenStreetMap. It was built for the Common Lot 404 page, which needed an on-brand empty-lot drawing from real data rather than a stock illustration. Use it to redraw that banner after a data refresh, as a starting point for any plat-style drawing of a single parcel and its block, or to pick parcels by shape and neighbor rules.
cl-block: Command that picks a half-mile square of central Kansas City and classes every lot in it as building, surface parking or vacant, tax break, or exempt, with property tax paid per acre for each class, written as SVG paths for a scroll story. It was built for the Common Lot home page to show downtown parking lots paying a fraction of the tax per acre that buildings pay. Use it to scan the city for the squares with the most idle land, to compare tax per acre on any block, or to make a parcel map for a talk or article.
cl-deploy: A shell script in the Common Lot repo that uploads dist/ and the Worker code to Cloudflare with wrangler, reading the account token from the repo's gitignored .env. It was created to publish the Common Lot site and its small API without a dashboard step. Use it after cl-site to publish a change, to redeploy the Worker after an API edit, or as a template for deploying another static site plus Worker.
cl-groupcheck: Measures how correctly Common Lot groups Kansas City parcels into owners. It draws a fixed random sample of merged owner groups and of pairs of separate groups, records a hash of the sample in git before any matcher change, and scores precision and recall once a person labels each item with evidence. It was made because the existing sample check only confirmed copied county values and nothing tested whether shell companies were merged or split correctly. Use it before and after a change to the owner matcher, to check an entity-resolution change against hand-traced ground truth, or to report a measured error rate for the owner rankings.
cl-heromap: Command that pulls every parcel outline in central Kansas City, simplifies the shapes, and groups them into west-to-east bands so a page can draw the map like a pen plotter, with idle and underused private land marked. It was built for the Common Lot hero animation after an architectural blueprint reference. Use it to make an animated or static parcel map of a district, or to cache central-city parcel shapes for other map work.
cl-landuse: Command that totals how Kansas City's land is used and what underuse costs: yearly land rent and the share property tax collects, idle land (vacant lots and surface parking), underused land (buildings worth less than half the land), abatement tax breaks, and the extra property tax idle and underused land would pay if built like its neighbors, citywide and per council district. It was built for the Common Lot site when the project moved from who owns land to how well land is used, a Georgist framing. Use it to get land value tax headline numbers for Kansas City, to compare council districts, or as the template for a land value capture estimate in another city with assessor data.
cl-linkcheck: A Python script in the Common Lot repo that checks every outside link on the live site with lychee, re-checks links that refuse tools in headless Chrome, and sends one notification listing any dead links. It was created to keep the City services directory honest, since stale phone numbers and links are the main failure of resource lists. Use it weekly through its launchd job, after editing services.json, or adapt it to watch links on another site.
cl-live: Command that builds the animated single-file mockup of the Common Lot site, inlining fonts, data, GSAP and Lenis so it opens in a sandboxed preview, with an optional headless scroll-through that saves review frames. It was built to review scroll-driven motion without running a web server. Use it to rebuild the mockup after a data refresh, to capture frames for design review, or as the pattern for any self-contained animated HTML page.
cl-mockup: Command that builds static Material Design mockups of the Common Lot home and About pages from the computed owner data, then renders desktop and phone screenshots in headless Chromium through a throwaway local web server. It was made so a design brief could be reviewed with real data before the production site exists. Use it to preview a page change, to make screenshots for a design review, or as the pattern for rendering pages that load ES module scripts.
cl-owners: Command that groups Kansas City parcels into real owners and ranks the top 100 by idle land, underused land, tax breaks and land value, with a separate list of public owners. It joins shell companies that share a mailing address and name family, keeps tax agents and IRA custodians from merging strangers, counts exemptions as tax breaks only inside abatement districts, and applies a naming rule that hides small individual owners. Use it to answer who holds the most vacant or underused land in the city, who gets the biggest abatements, or to find the owner group behind one property.
cl-pull: Command that pulls Kansas City, Missouri public land data into newline JSON files with a freshness manifest: parcels, code cases, vacant and Land Bank parcels, abatement districts and the parcels inside them, council districts checked against Legistar, school districts and census tracts with their parcels, the city's 2021 parcel snapshot, and FHFA tract land prices. It was built for the Common Lot land transparency site after the city's open data portal turned out to be stale while the GIS server behind the Parcel Viewer stays current. Use it to refresh land ownership data, to find which parcels sit in a district or tract, or as the paging pattern for any ArcGIS REST layer.
cl-ratio: Command that runs a sales ratio study of the assessor's values in the IAAO style with the open-source assesspy package: median ratio, COD, PRD and PRB by home type, council district and price quartile, plus vacant land, plus a sold-versus-unsold test that compares value changes since the 2021 roll for homes that sold and homes that did not. It was built to test whether the assessed values behind Common Lot's land measures are sound, and it is how sales chasing in the 2023 reassessment was found. Use it to audit an assessment roll, to support a property tax appeal argument with neighborhood statistics, or to repeat the study when the county releases its full sales file.
cl-report: Command that builds the sales-chasing evidence report as a PDF working paper: summary figures, four charts drawn as plain SVG, the IAAO tests, the explanations ruled out, limits and next steps, with every number computed from the pulled county data through the same shared module the ratio study prints from. It was built so the finding on Jackson County's 2023 values could go to reviewers and the Assessment Department in a form that reruns unchanged when the county's own sales file and 2025 roll arrive. Use it to refresh the report after new data, as the template for a reproducible data-journalism methods paper, or to make a print-ready PDF from computed results with clickable sources.
cl-sales: Command that pulls recorded sale prices for Kansas City parcels in Jackson County from the county's public real estate sales search, walking parcel-number prefixes one page at a time and dropping owner names on the way in. It was built for a sales ratio study of the assessor's values after the state's own ratio study for the county showed no data. Use it to get sale prices for a neighborhood, to rebuild the sales file after the county updates its search, or as the pattern for paging an old ASP.NET search form politely.
cl-sample: A Python script in the Common Lot repo that checks a random, seeded sample of the published owner rankings against Jackson County's own parcel table, comparing owner of record and assessed values. It was built as the outside check before the site went public, so the error rate comes from the county's records rather than the city's copy. Use it after any data refresh, before publishing new rankings, or to measure how far the city's parcel file drifts from the county's.
cl-shelter: Command in the Common Lot repo that builds the data behind the shelter zoning map: every Kansas City parcel where the zoning code permits Group Living (B and O districts) or allows it with a special use permit (DC, DX, DR, M1 and the dense R districts). It overlays parcel outlines with zoning, FEMA flood zones, historic register, overlay, incentive and planning case layers from the city GIS, building footprints from Overture Maps, the transit schedule and the city's shelter bed inventory, and writes GeoJSON for the map. It was built when a question about where shelters or encampments could legally go needed a parcel-level answer instead of a district summary. Use it to refresh the shelter map, to find land where a use is permitted by the zoning tables, or as the pattern for any parcel-by-parcel overlay of city GIS layers.
cl-shelter-check: Command in the Common Lot repo that checks the shelter zoning map against records it was not built from. It compares each parcel's zoning with the zoning field the city keeps on vacant parcels, tests known control sites, and draws a contact sheet of random parcels over the city's 2024 aerial photos so a person can grade the built-or-vacant call and store the counts. It was built so the map could publish its own error rates. Use it after every shelter map refresh, before the page goes public, or as a template for checking any land classification against aerial imagery.
cl-site: A Python build script in the Common Lot repo that writes the deployable site into dist/: the land page, the Meetings and City services pages, the 404 page, hashed asset files, security headers, robots and sitemap, and a social card image. It replaced the single-file mockup build when the site went to a public Cloudflare Worker, so assets could be cached and inline scripts forbidden. Use it before every deploy, to switch between the noindex preview and the public build, or as a pattern for a static site with strict headers on Cloudflare.
cl-streetcar-map: Draws the cl-streetcar-units result as one self-contained HTML map with MapLibre inlined and OpenFreeMap tiles. It shows the streetcar line, the stops, and each building colored by rent or own, with filters, a list and a popup of the context columns. It was built so the multifamily search can be read and shared as a single file. Use it again after a rerun of the finder, or as a template for any point dataset that needs a filterable map in one HTML file.
cl-streetcar-units: Finds residential buildings with 6 to 9 units within a quarter-mile walk of a Kansas City streetcar stop. It reads KCATA's GTFS stops, Jackson County parcel shapes and assessor rows, city zoning and Overture building footprints, and measures walk distance on the OpenStreetMap network. It was built to answer where small multifamily buildings sit along the streetcar, split into rentals and owner-held condos, with owner, value and zoning context. Use it again to shortlist small apartment buildings for sale or rent near transit, to count missing-middle housing in a transit corridor, or to change the unit range or walk radius for a different transit study.
cl-validate: Command that checks Common Lot's computed land and tax figures against records published by others: taxable assessed value and tax-break losses inside the Kansas City Public Schools district against the district's audited financial report, and assessor land values by census tract against the Federal Housing Finance Agency's appraisal-based land prices. It was built when the project moved from presenting numbers to proving them, so every headline figure has an outside check with a stated ratio. Use it after any data refresh, when a new school or city audit comes out, or as the template for validating a parcel analysis in another city against audited reports.
Claude Animation (song-sync): Fork of a p5.js and p5.brush watercolour animation kit whose song-sync command detects tempo and lyric cue times from a song so frames render in sync. Built to make hand-painted animated videos and music videos in code, locking visuals to a generated song instead of timing beats by hand. Making a music video for a generated track; rendering a short Clawd or cartoon clip; syncing lyric cues to a song with a known BPM.
Claude Home: Desktop app launching a live dashboard for home devices: electricity usage, HVAC, bedroom air quality, and the Nest doorbell, with bundled integrations that pull the data. Consolidates several home data sources into one viewer. It grew from an energy dashboard into a general home hub. Checking power usage or HVAC runtime at a glance; watching bedroom CO2; opening the doorbell feed.
claude-api-gate: Decides whether a claude session may use the Anthropic API key instead of the Claude plan. It reads the plan's 5-hour and weekly utilization from the account usage endpoint and opens only when one of them is at 100%, failing closed on any error. It was built so that the monthly API credits act as a strict last-resort fallback, never as a second default. Use it when a script that runs claude must survive the plan limit, when you need to see the plan's live 5-hour or weekly numbers from a shell, or when you are wiring a new headless runner that must never touch the API key on its own.
claude-spend: Estimates what local Claude Code usage would cost at API rates by scanning session transcripts, deduplicating messages and pricing tokens per model per month. Built to see the API-equivalent cost of Claude Code use, since one response is logged once per content block and needs deduping to count correctly. Checking monthly spend; comparing model cost; updating rates when pricing changes.
claude-stable-path: Bash script that pins the auto-updating claude CLI to one unchanging path so macOS TCC permissions, especially Full Disk Access, survive each release. Each CLI release lands at a new versioned path and TCC keys grants by path, so grants died roughly daily. This fixes that at the path level. Re-running after a CLI update breaks file access; checking that the stable path still resolves; debugging Full Disk Access loss for headless Claude runs.
Clippy Meme: Native app shell around the local paperclip meme generator served on port 5031 by launchd, wrapped in the shared app-shell WKWebView. Built so the Clippy-style meme generator opens as a normal Mac app instead of a browser page. Making a Clippy meme image; exporting a PNG from the generator; checking the paperclip-meme launchd service is up.
cloud-sync: The Mac's half of the fantasy cloud fallback, called by lineup-watch every 15 minutes: it sends a heartbeat to the fantasy-hub Worker, uploads the playbook, skill and watchlist when they change, and takes back what cloud routines edited, only as fast-forwards. coffee-order: Places or tests one pickup order at a Square Online coffee shop from headless Chrome, using a Chrome profile that is signed in to Square Pay and the shared page script from the Coffee iPhone app. It was made as the Mac fallback for the Coffee app, for when the phone cannot run the checkout. Use it to order a drink from the Mac, to run a no-charge test of the checkout with --dry-run, or as a model for driving any Square Online store's cart and checkout.
com.alexhedtke.dubpace: Daily launchd job that runs dubpace-update.sh to fetch new One Pace dub episodes from Pixeldrain, rename them to Plex format, place them in season folders, and trigger a Plex scan. Created to keep the self-hosted dub library current without manual downloads, resuming across runs because Pixeldrain rate-limits. Checking why new dub episodes are missing; running a backfill by hand; diagnosing a failure when the external SSD is unreachable.
com.alexhedtke.dubsubs: Hourly job that runs subgen.sh to transcribe One Pace dub episodes with whisper.cpp large-v3, post-correct them with a glossary, and write English sidecar subtitles for Plex. Built to give the self-hosted dub library subtitles without paying for a service, using cached raw transcripts so glossary changes are cheap to reapply. Adding subtitles to newly downloaded dub episodes; fixing a recurring mistranscription; checking batch progress by season.
com.alexhedtke.passage: KeepAlive launchd job serving Passage, a Flask paywall remover with rail-race fetching, reader mode, a freeze cache, and a library of cleaned pages. Keeps the paywall reader always available at a local port so any article link can be opened cleanly. Reading a paywalled article; checking that the Passage server is up; opening the library of cleaned pages.
com.alexhedtke.plex: launchd job that runs Plex Media Server through plex-guard.sh only while the external media drive is mounted, at login and on every volume mount. Built so Plex does not start against a missing library when the media SSD is unplugged, and starts itself when it is plugged in. Debugging why Plex is not running; changing which drive it depends on; understanding the mount-triggered start.
com.exobrain.5etools-server: Launchd job that keeps a local 5etools D&D reference site running by executing npm run serve:dev in the 5etools folder at load. Appears to have been set up so the self-hosted 5etools data and homebrew are always available offline for D&D work. Looking up spells, monsters, or items during play; testing homebrew content; restarting the server after an update.
com.exobrain.airdrop-console: Every-15-minute launchd job running a Python watcher that picks up things AirDropped to the Mac and delivers them to a MIST Console chat. Appears to exist so photos and files sent from the phone reach MIST without opening a chat manually. Debugging an AirDrop that never showed up in the console; adjusting the polling interval; checking whether the watcher is running.
com.exobrain.appliances-poll: Every five minutes polls LG ThinQ appliance state and writes appliances-data.json for the Claude Home dashboard panel. Appears to have been built so the home dashboard can show washer and dryer state from the official ThinQ API, following the Evergy and Nest pattern of one writer and a read-only app. Debugging a stale Appliances panel; adding another appliance brand; checking cycle status from data.
com.exobrain.asp-baton-watch: Every-6-hour launchd job that polls retailer product pages for one specific tactical baton model and alerts Alex on Discord when a price falls below a threshold. Built to catch a price drop on one exact SKU without checking stores manually, after an audit found some target pages served the wrong model. Checking the watcher is alive; adjusting the alert price; adding a retailer URL pinned to the exact SKU.
com.exobrain.auto-commit-harness: Nightly shell job that commits and pushes pending changes in the harness repo after a conservative filename-based gitignore check for secrets, runtime state and large binaries. Replaced a Claude routine that spent a full headless Opus session to do what a shell script can do; it is the mechanical backstop for auto-commit. Checking why changes were or were not committed overnight; adjusting the auto-ignore patterns; confirming the safety net ran.
com.exobrain.auto-update: Hourly launchd job that starts the automatic software update script, which does its work at most once a day on AC power in the early morning or when the Mac is idle. It replaced the absence of any scheduled upgrade, which left Homebrew packages months behind on security fixes. Look here when tools are unexpectedly out of date, when an upgrade happened at a strange time, or when deciding where to add a new package manager to the update sweep.
com.exobrain.awair-co2-watcher: Every 5 minutes it polls an Awair Element over the local API, logs CO2 and humidity to a CSV, and alerts by banner and Discord DM during active hours. Built to capture overnight air quality in the bedroom and warn when CO2 gets high, without middle-of-the-night notifications. Charting bedroom air quality; checking whether ventilation is adequate; debugging missing alerts or a gap in air-log.csv.
com.exobrain.awair-rollup: Nightly job running awair-rollup.py, which turns the CO2 and humidity time-series CSV into a daily Air Quality Log note in the Obsidian vault. Built to make raw Awair sensor readings into a readable per-day record, following the same pattern as the Energy Log. Checking daily CO2 or humidity trends; rebuilding the air quality note; diagnosing a night with no rollup.
com.exobrain.backup: Daily 02:00 job that builds one collective tarball of the harness, the Obsidian vault and every repo's gitignored files, uploads it to Google Drive, and prunes with grandfather-father-son retention. GitHub holds code but not secrets, databases or the vault, so this creates one atomic restore point for everything else. Restoring after data loss; verifying last night's backup ran; changing retention; checking that a new gitignored file is covered.
com.exobrain.backup-resume: Every-30-minute launchd job that runs backup-exobrain.sh to build one tarball of the harness, the vault, and gitignored repo data, upload it to Drive, and prune by retention. Created as a single atomic restore point for everything GitHub does not hold; the frequent schedule lets an interrupted or slept run resume. Verifying the latest backup exists; restoring after data loss; changing retention or what the archive contains.
com.exobrain.bodyguard-weekly: Daily launchd job running the bodyguard weekly script, which refreshes breach data and builds a passive OSINT query plan, then posts a notification to review it. Built to keep a recurring check on Alex's public exposure, such as breaches and data brokers, without remembering to run scans. Reviewing the weekly exposure scan; checking the latest plan file in the logs; updating the security log after a scan.
com.exobrain.bounty-hunter: Every-10-minute Python watcher that polls vetted open-source bounty payers for fresh, low-competition bounties and alerts on Discord and as a Mac banner. It also watches submitted PRs for review activity. Built because public bounty boards are honeypot farms or are swarmed by bots within hours, so being first on a known-good payer is the only edge. In October 2026 the Algora payers stopped posting, and the source list moved to per-payer entries (Tenstorrent first). Use it to check whether a bounty alert was missed, to add or retire a payer, or to see the status of an open bounty PR.
com.exobrain.chat-watch: Every 10 minutes it checks ESPN Fantasy Chat for unanswered league threads and runs a headless Claude to reply, while direct messages are handed to Alex instead. Appears to exist so the fantasy league chat gets timely replies from MIST while private conversations stay with Alex. Debugging a missed or duplicate league chat reply; changing the daily reply cap; checking the log for a run that answered nothing.
com.exobrain.claude-bot: Always-on launchd job running the MIST Discord bot, a discord.py client with a command registry, SQLite storage, and pluggable modules. Built to give a few private Discord servers a MIST assistant, modeled on the open-source Fletcher bot without its cross-server machinery. Restarting the bot after a code change; checking why it is offline; adding a feature module or command.
com.exobrain.claude-cli-update: Launchd job running claude-cli-autoupdate.sh four times daily to update the Claude Code CLI and notify Alex when the version changes. Created because the Console discovers models by reading the claude binary, so a stale CLI is the only reason a new model would fail to appear. When a new model is missing from the picker; after an update breaks a hardcoded path; adjusting update frequency.
com.exobrain.claude-stable-path: Job that pins the Claude Code CLI to one unchanging path whenever a new version lands, so macOS TCC permissions keyed by path survive updates. The CLI updates about daily to a new versioned path, which orphaned its Full Disk Access and other grants and caused a flood of permission prompts. Investigating recurring permission dialogs after a Claude update; checking the stable symlink; debugging launchd jobs that call claude.
com.exobrain.common-lot-linkcheck: A weekly launchd job that runs the Common Lot link checker on Mondays at 09:15 and alerts on any dead link. It exists so the City services page cannot drift out of date without anyone noticing. Use it as the reminder to fix dead links, check its log when a link alert arrives, or copy it for another weekly site check.
com.exobrain.comp-hunter: Every-6-hour launchd job polling Zindi, Apart Research sprints, Kaggle, and DrivenData for prize competitions and alerting on winnable ones. Second pipeline in the money portfolio: chase pre-funded competitions an agent can work on, with AI-safety sprints flagged for Alex's background. Reviewing new competitions; tuning the minimum prize or deadline filter; adding a competition source.
com.exobrain.cowork-sync: Five-minute launchd job running cowork-sync, which keeps the harness CLAUDE.md and the iCloud Claude Cowork copy identical in both directions by hash. Built because iCloud stores symlinks as tiny objects, so the cloud side must be a real file that is kept in step with the canonical one. Editing CLAUDE.md and needing the Cowork copy updated; diagnosing a sync conflict where both sides changed; running with --status.
com.exobrain.day-zero-watch: Every 30 minutes it snapshots a Facebook page counting down 3000 days, archiving text and screenshots and alerting on the countdown ending, a new payload post, or the page vanishing. Built to preserve whatever the page posted at zero in case it was deleted, with alerts as a secondary function. Reviewing the archive after the countdown ended; reusing the pattern to archive another page likely to disappear.
com.exobrain.deathcafe-kc-watch: Job polling a local Death Cafe host's event profile and the public library's Death Cafe pages every 12 hours. It alerts Alex on Discord when a new host event appears, adds it to Google Calendar with that event's own page as the link, and writes each library session's own page link into the matching instance of the recurring library series. Built so Alex learns the moment the next monthly session is scheduled and every calendar entry opens the exact event page, since dates post only weeks ahead. Confirming the watcher still runs; fixing a calendar entry that has a generic link; adapting the pattern to another event listing; checking which dates it has seen.
com.exobrain.dhs-ia-watch: Launchd job running a headless Claude that finds the newest teleconference invite in Gmail and writes the fresh Teams link and passcode into that calendar event. Built because the agency issues a new meeting link for every biweekly call with no recurring invite, making a bare calendar hold useless. Missing connection details on the call day; changing the search window or run times; reusing the pattern for another meeting series with rotating links.
com.exobrain.diesel-bike-watch: Twelve-hourly watcher that polls motorcycle listing sites for diesel motorcycles and alerts on any listing ID it has not seen before. Roughly one diesel motorcycle is on the market worldwide at a time, so there is no fixed product URL to price and discovery of new listings is the goal. Adding a listing source; checking the seen-listing state; debugging why an alert did or did not fire.
com.exobrain.discord-digest: Every-4-hour launchd job that waits for network and runs the Discord digest fetch of the friend group server for the briefing to summarize. Feeds the daily briefing's Discord section so plans and events from friends are not missed. Debugging a stale digest; checking the fetch logs; changing the digest cadence.
com.exobrain.eject-assist: Always-running launchd job that watches diskarbitrationd for failed volume ejects and frees the busy volume by asking what holds it to quit, then ejects. Built so clicking eject on an external drive works even when background processes hold it open. It never forces an unmount or kills a process; a holder that will not quit leaves the volume mounted and is named in the notification. Ejecting the Extreme SSD or another external volume; investigating what blocks an eject; running disk_eject.py free manually.
com.exobrain.energy-pull: Daily 06:30 job that waits for network, pulls Evergy electricity usage, then loads Evergy and Nest data into the energy.db warehouse. Built so cost, per-floor HVAC runtime and weather history stay joinable and current, after early pulls were lost when the Mac woke without Wi-Fi. Analyzing power bill drivers; checking whether yesterday's usage landed; debugging a missed pull in the energy log.
com.exobrain.envelope-budget-sync: Launchd job running sync_cli.py four times daily, the same sync as the envelope budget app's Refresh button, without the web server. Built so budget data stays current without Alex opening the app. Diagnosing stale budget numbers; checking sync results before a money question; changing how often it refreshes.
com.exobrain.fantazine-post-watch: A one-shot launchd watcher that posts a prepared thread on a ProBoards forum once a newly registered account is approved by the forum's staff. It reads the account status from the ProBoards account selector, posts with a persistent headless browser profile, verifies the thread went live, notifies with the link, and unloads itself. It was built to post a request for lost tabletop RPG downloads on a gamebook fan forum that holds new accounts for manual approval. Reuse it for any ProBoards forum post that has to wait on moderator approval, or as the template for a scheduled post on any site behind a proof-of-work bot wall.
com.exobrain.fantazine-replies-watch: A launchd watcher that checks one ProBoards forum thread, across all its pages, plus the account's private-message inbox, and alerts when someone other than the account owner replies or a new conversation appears. It reuses the signed-in headless browser profile of the posting watcher and sends one banner and Discord DM per run, with the reply text framed as untrusted data. It was built to catch answers to a request for lost tabletop RPG downloads on a gamebook fan forum. Reuse it to follow any forum thread or inbox where replies are rare and easy to miss, such as a want-to-buy post, a support thread, or a request to a long-time collector.
com.exobrain.fitbit-token: Launchd job running token-check.mjs four times daily to exercise the Fitbit OAuth token through the MCP server's own refresh path and raise a notification if re-auth is needed. Made so a broken refresh chain surfaces as a banner rather than a dark health pipeline discovered during the morning briefing. Health pulls fail with auth errors; checking whether the Fitbit token is warm; triggering the reauth flow.
com.exobrain.framesdirect-return-watch: Hourly launchd watcher that reads the local Gmail mirror Maildir for new mail about one online order return and raises a banner when any arrives. Built because the retailer's return status page needs a login and the carrier tracking page blocks scripted access, so the order and refund emails are the only readable signal. Use it to follow a return or refund to completion, as a template for any watcher keyed on incoming mail, or to check whether a retailer has confirmed receipt.
com.exobrain.gatorade-watch: Three-hourly watcher that polls retailer pages for a specific Gatorade flavor and sends a Discord message when one flips from sold out to buyable. Built because the product is often sold out and checking retailer pages by hand is tedious. Adding another retailer; investigating a missed restock; using it as a template for another stock watcher.
com.exobrain.gmail-mirror: Hourly launchd job that runs mbsync to pull the whole Gmail account (All Mail) into a local Maildir, then copies that Maildir to the external SSD when it is mounted. Built as a hedge against an unexplained Google account lockout, when Gmail had no copy anywhere outside Google. The mirror is append-only: server deletions never remove local mail. Use it to read old mail offline, to restore mail after losing the account, to grep years of email locally, or as the pattern for mirroring another IMAP account.
com.exobrain.haircut-check: Daily 10:00 launchd job that keeps two haircuts booked ahead at one salon and watches fallback bookings for a better time. It searches the salon's open slots in code and starts a headless MIST run only when a real candidate exists, so MIST can check the calendar, book, swap and notify. Built because the stylist books out months ahead and a short-lead nudge found nothing. Use it when checking why a cut was or was not booked, changing how far ahead to book, or debugging a swap that did not happen.
com.exobrain.headless-chrome-reaper: Two-minute shell job that kills only genuinely stuck headless Chrome render processes and their hung wrappers, gated on several signals so active renders survive. Built because headless Chrome dump-dom and screenshot calls can hang forever on macOS and pile up. Chrome processes eating memory; tuning the stuck thresholds; confirming concurrent renders in other sessions are safe.
com.exobrain.heartbeat-check: Daily 10:15 script that checks whether the day's routines produced their expected outputs and raises one banner listing anything missing or stale, with no model call. Replaced an older scheduled task; jobs that never ran say nothing themselves, so this checks outputs instead. Adding a check for a new routine; confirming morning jobs ran after the Mac slept; running with --dry-run to see verdicts.
com.exobrain.heilung-tour-watch: Job polling a Bandsintown-fed static mirror for tour dates, the band's official tour page and the band's RSS feed every 6 hours, alerting Alex on Discord. Alerts cover United States shows only: venues abroad and blog posts about tours abroad are logged without a ping, and the tour page status is logged only. Built so Alex hears of a new US tour announcement immediately, since the band posts mainly on social media that scripts cannot poll. Checking whether new US tour dates appeared; copying the multi-source pattern for another artist; fixing a false or repeated alert.
com.exobrain.imessage-sync: Every-15-minute launchd job running imessage-sync.py under a stable interpreter with Full Disk Access to snapshot the Messages database and contacts map into a cache. Created because Full Disk Access is granted per binary path and Claude Code's versioned path broke the grant on every update. iMessage searches return stale results; the Full Disk Access grant needs rebuilding; changing sync frequency.
com.exobrain.inbox-server: Launchd agent that keeps the Inbox clone's Flask server running on 127.0.0.1:5008 with KeepAlive, so the clone opens in any browser without the native window. Made so a plain browser bookmark to the clone always works, and so the snooze scheduler runs when the desktop app is closed. Use it when the Inbox bookmark does not load, when snoozed mail does not return, or when the desktop window and the browser must share one server.
com.exobrain.infragard-kc-watch: A launchd watcher that puts InfraGard Kansas City Members Alliance meetings on Google Calendar, with the Eventbrite event page as the RSVP link in each entry. It reads chapter announcement e-mail from the local Gmail mirror and pulls every Eventbrite link out of it, because the chapter publishes its meetings as unlisted Eventbrite events that never appear on its organizer page. It also checks the organizer page API for any listed event. Reuse it as the model for a group that announces private event links by e-mail, or for syncing any Eventbrite organizer's events into a calendar with dedup by event id.
com.exobrain.job-listings-sync: Job, run every five minutes and on file changes, that runs reconcile.py to keep job-listing note frontmatter consistent in the Obsidian Job Listings folder. Appears to have been built so listing status fields stay consistent after edits without doing manual frontmatter cleanup. Debugging a listing whose status did not update; changing the reconcile rules; checking that the sync is running.
com.exobrain.job-scan: Daily 09:00 launchd job running the headless job-search discovery scan across email alerts, scripted boards, LinkedIn, and other lanes, filtered by hard gates and deduped. Automates daily job discovery during a job search, replacing manual board checking, and notifies only on new verified candidates. Investigating a missed or empty scan day; checking new listing notes; changing a gate or lane.
com.exobrain.kcurbex-watch: Twelve-hour launchd job that runs an unattended pass over the KC Urbex forum, pacing requests gently because the board is a small volunteer site. Built so new site reports and meetups from the forum reach Alex without manual checking. Reviewing the latest urbex pass; checking why a report or meetup was missed; not raising the request rate.
com.exobrain.kqi-firmware-watch: The launchd entry that runs kqi-firmware-watch every day at 10:15 through mist-launch. It checks NIU's update cloud for new KQi Air scooter firmware and alerts once per new image or dead login. It replaced a manual 'kqi firmware pull' rerun. Use it when you need to know if the scooter firmware watch runs, or to change its schedule.
com.exobrain.lineup-watch: Every 15 minutes it checks the fantasy lineup for OUT, IR, bye, empty or questionable starters before lock and notifies, with --fix making verified swaps for definite problems. Built so a fantasy lineup problem gets caught and repaired before kickoff without Alex checking manually. Debugging a missed lineup ping or unexpected swap; adjusting the ping window; checking that the Mac stays awake before a lock.
com.exobrain.loki-poll: Hourly job polling the PetKit cloud for the litterbox and logging the cat's per-visit weight, time, and duration, plus a daily Obsidian note. Built because litterbox frequency and weight drift are early warnings of cat health problems, ahead of visible symptoms. Checking the cat's weight trend; investigating an unusual visit pattern; re-running discovery after the PetKit API changes.
com.exobrain.mac-studio-512-watch: A one-shot launchd watcher that reads the Apple Mac Studio configurator page with plain HTTP and parses the memory options from the JSON in the page. It was made to catch the day the M5 Ultra 512 GB memory option becomes orderable, for the price check on a local model server. It sends one banner and Discord DM, then removes itself from launchd. Use it as a template to watch any Apple Store configurator for a new option, a price change, or a footer note that changes.
com.exobrain.mem-watchdog: Always-on launchd daemon that reads the kernel's memory pressure level, the compressor thrash rate and every process's footprint, kills sustained runaway processes (with a fast lane for memory-hungry search tools), and alerts through mist-notify on pressure transitions and on a process that is growing, not just one that is big. It also asks the MIST Console to reload its page when the web view leaks past a threshold and measures whether that freed memory. Built after runaway apps and a grep regex blowup exhausted the 8GB Mac's RAM and froze it, leaving no record of the culprit; rewritten (v4, 2026-10-11) after its swap alert fired hourly for weeks and its notifier calls failed silently. Investigating a freeze or slowdown; reading which process was killed or reloaded and why; changing warn, growth, kill or pressure thresholds or the protected list.
com.exobrain.missing-person-candidate-ra: Daily job that runs mp-rate for the past seven days and notifies with how often the missing-person news-candidate track fires. The candidate threshold was set from one cold-start sample, so this measures the steady-state firing rate to check whether the threshold is right. Reviewing whether the two-agreement threshold needs tuning; checking watcher health; looking at candidate volume over time.
com.exobrain.missing-person-watch: Daily 08:15 launchd job running the missing-person toolkit's watch command for one specific case to check databases and news. Automates daily monitoring of the sources that would change first if the person were found or new information appeared. Checking that the daily case watch ran; reviewing the latest watch output; pausing it when the case closes.
com.exobrain.mist-console-autocommit: Thirty-minute shell job that commits and pushes the private MIST Console repo, including conversation history, and does nothing when the tree is clean. Built so Console chat data and local edits stay synced without manual commits. Confirming Console changes reached the remote; debugging a failed push; adding paths that should not be committed.
com.exobrain.mist-console-watch: Every minute it checks that the MIST Console answers on port 5014 and reopens the app through LaunchServices if not. Built so the Console recovers after a crash, quit or login and the phone can reach the Mac whenever it is on. Investigating why the Console keeps reopening; verifying it is running after a restart; changing the recovery or restart guard behavior.
com.exobrain.mist-duel-brain: Always-on decision server for the MIST Yu-Gi-Oh bot, answering the game executor's requests through a live Claude session or fallback backends. Built so MIST reasons through each duel decision herself, with a heuristic fallback so a stalled reader does not hang the game. Playing a duel against MIST; debugging a stalled duel; switching the decision backend.
com.exobrain.mist-hotkey-agent: Always-on accessory-mode macOS agent that listens for a double-tap Option gesture and shows a glowing quick-entry overlay over any app, including fullscreen ones. Built as a separate process because only an Accessory app can float over fullscreen apps, and the console's own window would lose its fullscreen if it changed policy. The hotkey or overlay stops responding; changing the gesture; debugging quick entry into a new MIST chat.
com.exobrain.mist-studio: Keep-alive job that runs the MIST Studio server, a local Suno-style song studio at port 5032 for generating, covering, repainting and splitting tracks. Keeps the local music studio available at all times as an alternative to a paid song generation service. Generating a song; covering an uploaded track; restarting the studio server; checking its log.
com.exobrain.mount-reminders: Every-10-minute and on-mount launchd job that shows one banner when a named volume is mounted and a reminder file for it has content. Lets Alex leave a note for work to do when an external drive is plugged in, such as a queued backup. Queuing a task for the next time a drive mounts; clearing a reminder after finishing; debugging a missing banner.
com.exobrain.mychart-sync: A launchd job that runs mychart sync three times a day (07:30, 13:30, 19:30) through the mist-launch launcher, with writes and prompts turned off. It copies every MyChart account into the local store and sends one counts-only banner and Discord digest when new lab results, care-team messages, bills, or appointment changes appear. It exists so new results surface without anyone opening a patient portal. Check it when a digest seems late, after a passkey change, or when the sync log shows sign-in failures.
com.exobrain.mykcmo-auto-updates: A daily launchd job that asks Kansas City 311 for an update on each of Alex's open reports that has had no movement and no update request for seven days, then sends one banner and one Discord message. It reads the city's own record of filed update requests, which the KC 311 iPhone app shares, so the two never ask twice. Look here when a 311 report seems stuck, when an automatic update alert arrives, or to change the seven-day rule.
com.exobrain.mykcmo-key-watch: A daily launchd job that checks the 311 app API key with one signed call and, when the city has rotated it, pulls the new key from the latest app build, rebuilds and reinstalls the KC 311 iPhone app, and sends a banner and a Discord message. It replaced checking the key by hand after the 311 integration moved to the city app's backend. Look here when 311 filing breaks without warning, when a key-rotation alert arrives, or to see how often the key changes.
com.exobrain.mykcmo-watch-updates: A launchd job that checks Alex's Kansas City 311 reports every 5 minutes through the myKCMO app backend. When city staff change a report, or an update request that names it, the job sends the new timeline entries as one Mac banner and one Discord DM, which reaches the phone as a push. It was made because the city sends no push to unofficial clients and the iPhone app only gets background time when iOS allows it. Use it to know at once when a pothole, sidewalk, or other 311 case moves, to debug a missed ticket alert, or as the pattern for a watcher that diffs a case timeline.
com.exobrain.nest-events: Ten-minute Python job that drains Nest SDM HVAC events from Google Cloud Pub/Sub and updates exact per-floor runtime in nest-data.json. Built because five-minute polling missed cooling cycles and went blind while the Mac slept; queued events reconstruct overnight runtime. Energy and HVAC analysis; checking thermostat runtime after the Mac wakes; fixing Pub/Sub credential or subscription problems.
com.exobrain.nest-nightlog: Daily 08:00 job that writes a per-night log of third-floor overnight HVAC runtime next to the outdoor low into the Energy Log note. Built to separate savings from a changed thermostat schedule from merely mild nights, by holding weather constant. Judging whether the overnight schedule experiment is saving money; reviewing nightly runtime against outdoor lows.
com.exobrain.nest-poll: Job sampling the Google Nest thermostat API every 5 minutes, accumulating per-floor cooling and heating runtime into a store and the Energy Log note. Built because the API only reports live state, so runtime has to be sampled on a schedule and summed. Asking how long the AC ran per floor; correlating HVAC use with electricity cost; checking a gap in the log.
com.exobrain.nest-precool: Daily 14:00 job that sets per-floor Nest thermostat afternoon pre-cool depth from the day's forecast high, before the 4 to 8 pm peak rate window. Built to bank cold ahead of expensive peak hours on hot days and avoid wasted deep cooling on mild days, layered over the native Nest schedule. Tuning pre-cool tiers; investigating a warm afternoon; auditing electricity cost against HVAC runtime.
com.exobrain.nest-precool-log: Daily 8:10 PM launchd job that pairs each day's afternoon pre-cool decision with how long the compressor ran, end-of-peak comfort, and peak-window energy use. Created to close the loop on weather-responsive pre-cooling and learn whether a given bank depth was needed or wasted on a mild day. Reviewing whether pre-cooling saves money; tuning bank targets from accumulated days; checking a missing day in the log.
com.exobrain.nextdns-link: A launchd job that runs every 30 minutes and, only when the Mac's default gateway is the home TP-Link router, relinks the home public IP to the NextDNS TV profile through bin/nextdns. It exists because the Samsung TV reaches NextDNS over plain DNS, which NextDNS attributes to a profile by the caller's public IP, so a changed ISP address would stop the TV's queries from being logged or filtered. Use it as the pattern for any linked-IP NextDNS profile, or check its log when the TV profile's status shows a linked IP that does not match the home address.
com.exobrain.nudge-watch: The launchd job that runs the fantasy nudge watcher at 30-minute intervals. It was built for a business-idea panel that had to work without any of the operator's own context leaking in, then extended for a creative commission written and revised by a small team of model writers. Reach for it to evaluate business or product ideas, red-team a plan, or have a small team of independent model writers draft and revise a piece until they all sign it.
exposure_audit.py: Python scanner that checks staged git changes, a path, stdin or full git history for personal data, credential patterns and document metadata leaks, with exit codes by severity. Built for the cybersecurity-bodyguard skill to stop private data from being published in commits or public repos. Before a commit or push in a public repo; before making a repo public (--history); auditing a file before sharing it; wiring into a pre-commit hook.
fanedit-cc-align: Retimes a film's original closed captions onto a fan edit or recut of that film. It matches a word-level whisper transcript of the edit against the original subtitle files, finds each clip the editor used and its time offset, and moves every original caption (speaker labels and sound tags included) to its new position, so the text stays official and only the timing comes from whisper. Built to give a two-part fan edit of a film trilogy proper SDH captions for Plex, where neither raw whisper text nor a single global subtitle shift works. Use it for any fan edit, extended or reordered cut, or a recut that lost its subtitles; or to check whether a subtitle file matches a video.
fantasy consensus judge: Two-step script that builds a consensus board from CBS and FFToday full-PPR projections, then grades the draft room under both the bot's board and the consensus. Fixes a self-grading loop where the draft bot was graded on the same projections it drafted from, which flattered its own picks. After a draft or mock draft to check the build is robust; when changing draft bot valuations; comparing rank gap between our board and outside consensus.
fantasy correlation table: Python estimator of how fantasy players' weekly surprises move together: teammates, opponents, a defense against the offense it faces, by position and projection tier, from nflverse box scores against Sleeper's archived projections. Built so the lineup win probability stops treating starters as independent draws, which understated the spread of stacked lineups. Use it when pricing a QB-receiver stack, when a D/ST faces the opponent's quarterback, when calibrating any lineup or matchup simulation, or for DFS-style correlation questions.
fantasy disagreement ledger: Python CLI that logs places where the draft board disagrees with consensus as predictions, then settles them against actual ESPN season points. Built so board-versus-consensus disagreements get scored against reality instead of trusted on instinct, and only settled results feed back into the board. Recording a new disagreement during draft prep; settling predictions weekly in season; judging whether an elite-bias correction in the value model is real.
fantasy divergence signoff: CLI for the pre-draft gate that compares the draft board to FantasyPros consensus positional ranks, lists material divergences, and records each as a signed bet or a correction. Created after a rule that any counter-consensus pick needs an explicit thesis, since the board's divergences were coming from source noise rather than conviction. Before a draft after rebuilding the board; checking that no unsigned divergence remains on draft morning; signing a deliberate bet with a thesis or re-slotting a player to consensus rank.
fantasy draft examiner: Audits the fantasy draft autopilot's picks against FantasyPros expert consensus rankings, either replaying a simulated draft or reading the live draft. The autopilot and its simulator share the same value board, so they cannot catch board mistakes by agreeing with each other. This adds an outside yardstick. On draft morning after refreshing consensus data; checking a flagged pick during a live draft; testing board changes against consensus.
fantasy draft scoreboard: Python grader that scores every team in an open ESPN draft room on projected optimal starting lineup, using the same projections as the VOR board and Pick History data. Built to answer whether a drafted roster is good with a number instead of an eyeball, on the same scale the drafting bot optimizes. Mid-draft or right after a draft to rank all rosters; printing top rosters with --rosters N to learn from them; run before leaving the draft room.
fantasy draft simulator: Offline Python simulator that runs a 13-seat fantasy draft against ESPN auto-bot or crowd-ADP opponents and grades optimal starting lineups on ESPN projections. A live practice draft takes eight minutes and yields one seat's result, so this measures autopilot draft policies across all seats in under a second. Testing a draft policy change (for example whether to take a QB early); comparing seeds or opponent models; checking the sim still matches autopilot.js scoring.
fantasy draft supervisor: Python supervisor that owns the draft driver's command channel during a live fantasy draft, logging each pick to supervise.log and driving a progress bar from roster count. Created so nothing else races on the autopilot's result file while a draft runs, and so progress can be read from one log. Immediately after arming the draft autopilot; watching pick progress during a live draft; debugging a stalled draft driver.
fantasy fpranks judge: Python scorer and rank generator that grades weekly fantasy rankings with FantasyPros' published in-season accuracy method (rank slot to predicted points, accuracy gap over a pool of consensus and actual top players, penalties for ranked inactives). Built to give the fantasy system an outside judge, so MIST's projections are compared with the expert consensus on the contest's own rules instead of self-grading. Use it to score any set of weekly ranks, to save a kickoff snapshot of two rankers side by side, or to produce half-PPR ranks at contest depth for an entry.
fantasy injury table: Python table builder that joins ten seasons of NFL injury reports to snap counts and projections: the share of regular contributors who played by position, game status and practice participation, and how they scored against projection when they did. Built so the lineup check prices a questionable starter from measured odds instead of reading news text. Use it for start/sit calls on questionable players, for planning bye or injury cover, or for any question about how often a listed player sits.
fantasy market projection: Python model that turns sportsbook player prop lines (receiving yards, receptions, rushing and passing yards, kicking points) plus the implied team total into fantasy points on the league's own scoring, one linear fit per position. Built because every projection the weekly forecast used came from another site, and the betting line is the rawest forecast with money behind it; it ties Sleeper and beats ESPN out of sample. Use it to add a market vote to a weekly projection, to check closing line value of a forecast, or to price a start/sit call when the books have moved after the projection sites last updated.
fantasy nflraw: Python data layer that scores nflverse box scores on the fantasy league's exact rules (full PPR, 4-point passing TD, distance-weighted kicking, D/ST points and yards allowed brackets) and joins schedules with closing lines, the cross-site player id table and Sleeper's archived weekly projections. Built so every model reads one scoring function that matches ESPN to the decimal instead of each script re-deriving it. Use it for any backtest of a fantasy rule, for residual or calibration studies, or when a past week's points are needed for players who were never on a league roster.
fantasy opportunity overlay: Python script computing 2025 volume metrics and touchdown-regression flags via nflreadpy, writing draftbot/opportunity.json for the draft sheet. Built to flag players whose touchdowns are out of line with their volume, so buy and sell candidates surface before the draft. Rebuilding before the draft after late-preseason data updates; hunting BUY or SELL thesis candidates; checking a player's volume versus scoring.
fantasy role model: Python projection model built from opportunity alone: team pass and rush volume from the closing spread and total, player target, carry and snap shares from a discounted Beta-Binomial filter with partial pooling, and points per opportunity shrunk to the position mean. Built to test whether a Bayesian role model adds to the Sleeper and betting-market projections; walk-forward on 2022-2025 it did not, so it is a research artifact. Use it as a baseline for a new projection idea, for questions about how fast a role change should move a projection, or as a template for discounted conjugate updating.
fantasy season_sim: A Monte Carlo of the fantasy league season from the real rosters and the real schedule: it plays the remaining weeks thousands of times, seeds the playoffs by win percentage then points for, and reports each team's playoff, first-round bye and title odds. It was built to price the season objective (the bye) instead of judging standings by eye, and it replaced a hand count of records. Its --leverage report reruns the season with one change at a time to price each lever: the title odds at each seed with the team held fixed, a win in each remaining week, a point of Points For, and a point in each week including the playoff weeks, which gives the per-week weights for valuing players. Use it for the Tuesday bye-odds update, for 'how do we stack up' questions, to price a rival's game with --force, and whenever a rule has to weigh wins against points or the regular season against the playoffs.
fantasy trade_scan: Enumerates every 1-for-1 and 2-for-1 trade with each rival, scores both lineups on projections, and runs the best through a paired season simulation for title and playoff odds. Built to find trades that raise the league title odds and that another manager could plausibly accept, instead of scanning trade options by eye. Weekly trade evaluation; checking whether a rival offer helps both sides; looking for belief-based trades where the board and ESPN projections disagree.
fantasy vor board: Python script that builds a value-over-replacement draft board from ESPN projections in league scoring crossed with The Ringer's positional ranks, written to draftbot/vor.json. Created so the draft bot and Alex pick by value over replacement at each position, not by raw rank, for the league's size and scoring. Rebuilding the board the morning of a draft; changing replacement-level assumptions for a different league; feeding draft-day tooling with fresh values.
fantasy-cloud-deploy: Deploys the fantasy-hub Cloudflare Worker through the Workers API with no wrangler: the script, its KV binding, its secrets and a 15-minute cron trigger. It was built so the fantasy watchers and routines keep running when the Mac is off; the Worker watches the Mac heartbeat and starts the GitHub Actions fallback. Use it to redeploy after a change to worker.js, to push fresh ESPN cookies to the cloud, or as the pattern for another Worker that needs KV and secrets.
fantasy-cloud-run: Sets up and closes a fantasy routine inside a cloud Claude session: start gates the run on the Mac heartbeat, the local time slot and once a day, then puts the ESPN cookies, playbook and skill at their Mac paths; finish sends changed files back to the hub with their base hash. It exists so the Mac's Fable routines have a cloud twin when the laptop is off. Use it when adding another cloud routine, when debugging a cloud run that skipped, or as the pattern for running any Mac-bound routine in the cloud.
fb: Read-only Facebook CLI that uses cookie-auth Playwright and GraphQL capture to crawl, parse and report on any group, page or profile, with top-N and by-year outputs. Built as a general toolkit to pull and rank Facebook group history without reacting, commenting or posting.
