Finding a group; crawling a group feed and building a ranked report; author leaderboards; refreshing cookies when the session dies.
fb refresh-cookies: Subcommand of the fb CLI that re-exports Facebook session cookies from the live Chrome or Brave profile by decrypting the browser's on-disk cookie store with the Keychain key. Appears to exist because the Facebook toolkit reads with a logged-in session and copied-profile browser launches cannot reuse the encrypted cookies. When fb reads start failing on auth; after logging into Facebook again in Chrome or Brave; testing the decrypt path with --dry-run.
fetch-assets: Downloads the third-party assets mist-vid needs into its gitignored assets folder: gl-transitions shaders, IM Fell and Cinzel Decorative fonts, the ambientCG Paper001 texture, Kenney RPG Audio and Impact Sounds, and the rife-ncnn-vulkan macOS binary with its v4.6 model. Created so the mist-vid repo carries only code, with licensed media fetched on demand. Run it after a fresh clone of the harness, when mist-vid reports a missing font, texture or RIFE binary, or when you need CC0 book page-flip and impact sounds for another project.
fetch-mascot: Shell script that downloads the mascot artwork from the original tool's site into the paperclip-meme repo as a gitignored local file. The art is not redistributed in the repo, so a fresh clone needs it fetched once. After cloning paperclip-meme; re-downloading a missing mascot file; using a different art URL.
ff: Read-only ESPN fantasy football CLI that reads the league through the ESPN v3 API using stored session cookies and surfaces the numbers the playbook uses. Built so lineup, waiver and trade decisions rest on live league data while writes stay in a separate gated tool. Checking rosters, standings or matchups; gathering data for start/sit, waivers or trades; preparing weekly decisions.
ff-dash: A local web dashboard for the current fantasy football week. It is served on port 5023 by a launchd job, and it logs the win probability each minute while games are on. It was built so that the lineup model's live odds have a page and a history. Before it, the only output was a single number from the command line. Use it to watch a live week, to see who is still to play and what a touchdown would do, to check the league scoreboard with model odds, or as the base for a backtest of the live probability.
fic-stats: Prints title, author, word count, summary, and popularity counts (AO3 kudos, hits, bookmarks; FFN favs, follows, reviews) for a list of fanfic URLs. It reads FicHub's cached metadata and the Wayback Machine's AO3 snapshots, because AO3 and FanFiction.net both refuse scripted requests. It was made to rank fics for a premise when AO3 was down after a security incident. Use it to rank candidate stories from a recommendation thread, to check how popular a story is, or to get a fic's summary and tags when AO3 or FFN cannot be reached.
fit-gate: Decides gate 4 (strong fit) for job listing notes from a per-JD-line scorecard table instead of a written impression. Each row records the level the job description asks for, the candidate's real level, and Met, Partial or Unmet; the script computes the score, fails knockouts, and can decline failed notes in place. It was built after a systems-administrator role passed as a strong fit at about half the real overlap because the audit matched topics rather than verbs. Use it when a scan or audit needs a fit verdict, to sweep the tracker for candidates that were never scored, or to re-check the pipeline after the capability table changes.
fitbit-mcp: Launcher for the forked Fitbit MCP server, which loads secrets from the harness environment and runs the compiled Node server over stdio. Exposes Fitbit data such as sleep, heart rate and activity to Claude tools, maintained as a fork with its own token handling. Registering or restarting the Fitbit MCP server; rebuilding after a missing build directory; debugging a token problem.
fitbit-reauth: Shell script that reruns the Fitbit browser consent flow to write a fresh token, using secrets from the gitignored harness .env. Needed when the refresh chain is broken and the token check reports NEEDS_REAUTH. Routine expiry refreshes itself. Health pulls failing on auth; after fitbit-token-check reports NEEDS_REAUTH; setting up Fitbit on a new machine.
fitbit-token-check: Shell entry point that runs the Fitbit MCP token health check under Node. Built to verify Fitbit OAuth tokens are healthy; launchd calls node directly to avoid a TCC block on shell wrappers. Health data pulls failing; checking token expiry manually; before a large Fitbit backfill.
flag-canary: Plants flag.txt canary files at the root of every directory this Mac exposes to the cloud (sync roots and served web roots) and deploys the Cloudflare Worker they point to. The file uses CTF framing: it tells an intruding AI agent that it passed the evaluation, asks it to submit the flag to the Worker, which sends a Discord DM, and then asks it to revert its changes and end the session. It was made as a tripwire for AI-driven intrusions, because an agent working under a CTF or eval story looks for exactly this file. Use it to add a new cloud-exposed folder or server as a target, to check that the canaries are still in place, to prove that the alert path works, or to rotate the token after a trip.
Flipper BLE: App bundle that runs the Flipper Zero Bluetooth script so macOS attributes Bluetooth permission to the bundle instead of a terminal or Console process. Bare Python launched from Claude or a terminal is killed by TCC for lacking Bluetooth permission. Wrapping it in a bundle fixed that. Any wireless Flipper operation: reading or writing device files, transmitting signals, inspecting state; not for USB use.
flipper-ble: Wrapper that runs the Flipper Zero Bluetooth script inside a Flipper BLE app bundle so macOS grants Bluetooth permission, supporting ping, list and write commands. Bare Python launched from Console or a terminal without a Bluetooth usage key is killed by TCC, so running inside a bundle makes the bundle the responsible process. Talking to the Flipper wirelessly; pushing an infrared file to the device; rebuilding the bundle after a permission problem.
forecast: Python CLI running the weekly 50 and 90 percent prediction loop for the fantasy team: dossier, record, settle, calibrate, history. Built so weekly forecasts are filed and scored against reality, keeping predictions calibrated over the season. Filing this week's forecast; settling last week's; checking calibration history.
freehire-lane: A discovery lane over the free freehire.me jobs API, which indexes iCIMS, UKG, ADP, Paycom, Workday, Greenhouse and other systems. It was added when a scan of other job-search tools found it covered ATSes no harness lane reached, and it returns parsed required JD lines and ghost-posting signals. Use it in the daily job scan, to draft fit-scorecard rows from a posting, or to spot mass-posted or fake-fresh listings.
freesound-pull: Downloads short sound effects from the Freesound API into the table-conductor library: for each one-shot tile in freesound.json it searches by query with a CC0 or CC BY license filter, saves the most downloaded HQ MP3 previews, and records author, license and URL for attribution. It was made to give the RPG audio player magic and monster one-shots that the CC0 game packs lack. Use it to add new sound effect tiles, to refresh a tile with better sounds, or as a template for any Freesound API pull that needs only a token and no OAuth.
gen_art.py: Python script that generates card art for every entry in the tarot deck's deck.json using mist-image, skipping existing files and reporting progress to the console. Built to bulk-generate the illustrations for a personal tarot deck project instead of prompting each card by hand. After adding cards to the deck; re-running for cards that failed; regenerating art after prompt changes.
geo: Geolocation toolkit CLI: latitude from shadow length, sun position, Street View coverage and capture date, GeoGuessr scoring, geocoding, Overpass queries, and sign enhancement. Built as the tool bench behind the geoguesser skill so location reads from photos rest on computed evidence, not guesses. Placing a photo from shadows or signs; checking whether Street View covers a spot; computing GeoGuessr score for a guess; upscaling a blurry sign.
geo-pano: Shell script that looks up Street View panorama coverage for a latitude and longitude with the streetlevel library through Google's internal API, no key needed. Split out of the geo tool so its dependency-free subcommands stay instant, with the EXIF dependency stubbed out. Checking whether Street View exists at a point; verifying a GeoGuessr location guess; finding coverage year near a coordinate.
Ghidra: Vendored NSA reverse-engineering suite run from a standalone zip, with analyzeHeadless for scripted batch analysis and ghidraRun for the GUI, needing JDK 21. Installed because the Homebrew cask needs sudo, which non-interactive shells cannot provide, so the release zip was downloaded to ~/tools instead. Disassembling or decompiling an unknown binary; batch-running a Ghidra script over imported files; inspecting a suspicious executable after static triage.
govee: A command-line tool that controls the Govee smart bulbs in the home over the local network, through the Govee LAN API and the open-source govee-local-api library. It finds the bulbs, reads their power, brightness, and color, and sets on/off, brightness, RGB color, and color temperature, with short aliases for each bulb. It was made when Alex installed Govee color bulbs, so that MIST can control the lights directly with no cloud round trip and no rate limit. Use it to change the room lights from a chat, to make a lighting cue for a routine (wind-down, wake-up, a focus timer), to show a status as a light color, or to do a check that the bulbs are online.
gphotos-embed: Bash script that rewrites a Google Photos share link to a Cloudflare Worker host so Discord shows a playable video, then copies the result to the clipboard. Built because Discord will not play Google Photos videos inline, following the way fxtwitter fixes X links. Sharing a Google Photos video in Discord; converting a link on the clipboard; pointing at a different worker host.
gphotos-embed-deploy: Bash script that uploads worker.js to Cloudflare Workers through the API, enables the workers.dev subdomain, and prints the worker URL. Discord will not play Google Photos videos inline. The worker rewrites share links so they embed, and this deploys it without wrangler. Redeploying the embed worker after an edit; rotating the worker name; verifying the live URL.
great-wheel-charting: The charting pipeline of The Great Wheel. It turns a sourcebook PDF into text in reading order, column by column, then checks and merges chart files (one JSON per crystal sphere, with bodies, orbits, looks, page cites and wiki links) into the map's atlas. Built to chart the Spelljammer crystal spheres from their books, in place of hand entry in the editor. Use it to chart a new sphere or plane from a book, to pull stat blocks out of any two-column TSR scan, or to bulk-import data into the atlas with validation.
great-wheel-map-mask: A script in the Great Wheel repo that turns a printed or fan-drawn world map into a land mask: each pixel is classed as sea, land or lava by color, labels and grid lines take the class of their nearest neighbor, and the result is a soft-edged equirectangular PNG. It was made so painted planets can take real coastlines from outline maps (Krynn, Patera) without pasting a labeled map on the globe. Use it to give any procedural planet canonical coastlines from a map image, to strip labels, borders and graticules out of a map before reuse, or to make a land/sea/lava mask for any equirectangular texture work.
gridpoint-build-install: Shell script that regenerates the Xcode project, does a clean signed Release build of the Gridpoint weather app, prints profile expiry, and installs it wirelessly to the paired iPhone. Stale build products skipped code signing and shipped an old embedded provisioning profile, so this forces a clean build and verifies expiry before install. Shipping a Gridpoint change to the phone; renewing its provisioning profile; diagnosing an app that refuses to launch after profile expiry.
gridpoint-monitor: Python script that logs NWS and Open-Meteo forecasts plus observed KMKC weather into SQLite every 30 minutes, with score.py reporting per-source accuracy. Built for the Gridpoint project to measure which weather source forecasts Kansas City most accurately, with append-only history so scores compare what was forecast at the time. Checking which forecast source to trust; running score.py for an accuracy report; debugging gaps in the forecast or observation log.
guard-identity: A Claude Code PreToolUse hook that stops web requests carrying the owner's email, phone, street address, or name in a header, and stops identity headers such as From or X-On-Behalf-Of. It was built after an agent was found sending the owner's email in User-Agent strings because API usage pages asked agents to identify their user. Use it as the reference when a site asks for a contact in the User-Agent, when debugging an unexpected permission prompt on a web request, or when adding a new identifier that must never leave the machine.
hand-letter: uv script that draws text as pen strokes using Hershey stroke fonts with per-letter wobble, tilt, pressure and felt-tip texture, saved as a transparent PNG or over a base image. Built to make handwritten-looking text for images and video where a typed font looks wrong. Adding a handwritten caption to an image; making a note or sign look hand-drawn; generating overlay lettering for animation.
harness-commit: Bash script that stages, privacy-audits, injection-scans, commits, and pushes the public harness repo, with a dry-run mode. Created as the only sanctioned commit path for unattended routines, so a fooled session cannot publish unchecked text to a public repo. Any routine or session that needs to commit the harness; previewing with --dry-run; investigating a scanner or privacy audit rejection.
Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone: Native Apple Silicon build of the 2001 PC game using a patched SurrealEngine (Unreal Engine 1 reimplementation) rendered through Vulkan and MoltenVK, with notes and scripts. Appears to be a project to play the old Windows game on an M1 Mac without Wine, after Wine-based attempts fell short. Launching the game; continuing porting work on later levels; reproducing the setup from its README and download manifest.
heal-python-stubs.sh: Script that repairs dedicated Python interpreter stubs after a Homebrew patch upgrade by recopying the stub, rewriting its framework path to the stable opt path, and re-signing it. Homebrew deletes the versioned Cellar path on patch upgrades, which broke stubs that hold macOS privacy grants and took dependent sync jobs down. After brew upgrades break iMessage sync or permission carry-forward; healing stubs without running them.
hiker-mealplan: An integer-programming menu optimizer over the Hiker Food Chart spreadsheet. It picks whole servings of foods and dried meals that meet calorie, protein, carb-to-protein, fat, sugar, fiber and sodium targets at the lowest total pack weight. It was built to plan the lightest vegan backpacking day from the filtered chart. Use it to plan trail food for a trip, to see how much weight a macro limit costs, or to rerun a plan after the chart data changes.
hitpoints-verify: Python script that pulls Fitbit sleep nights and daily steps, marks each night goal-met or not, merges results into the Ironman log, and emits level-up events. Built so the Hitpoints skill in the Ironman life-tracking app reflects measured Fitbit data instead of self-reported claims. Refreshing Hitpoints after syncing the watch; checking the last 14 nights; running with --dry-run or a different sleep goal.
Home Assistant: Desktop app launcher that runs ha_desktop.py from the home-assistant project's virtualenv. Appears to be a native window for the home automation project so it can be opened from the Dock. Opening the home control interface; checking smart home devices; developing in the home-assistant project.
hp1-actor-dumps: Turns the dumpactors lines in a native HP1 engine log into a per-actor table of state, location, velocity, acceleration and destination over time. It was built to find NPCs that stop against walls in the Harry Potter port, where a student that shows the same location with a non-zero acceleration in every dump is stuck. Use it to check crowd or patrol behavior after a physics change, to find which character never reaches its goal in a level, or to compare NPC movement between two engine builds.
hp1-camera-log: A Python script in the HP1 macOS port repo that reads a test run log and prints, for each sample time, where the follow camera is relative to Harry: horizontal distance, height, the angle from directly behind him, and the actor the camera's position check last hit. It was made to diagnose a report that the follow camera sat in the wrong place, which turned out to be the camera script pulling itself into Harry at invisible blocking walls. Use it to check camera behavior after an engine change, to find where a scripted controller route puts the camera too close, or to compare camera placement between two builds.
hp1-check-staged: Exports the git index of the HP1 port's engine checkout to a scratch folder and runs clang -fsyntax-only on the named files with the build's own defines, includes and flags. It was made to split one mixed working tree of engine changes into several commits that each compile, without rebuilding the binary that a long smoke test was using; before it, each split was checked by hand with ad hoc snapshot folders. Use it when you stage part of a file with grepdiff and want to know the staged state compiles, when you reorder or split commits in the engine repo, or as a quick compile check while a test holds the build folder.
hp1-fn: Prints decompiled functions from a Ghidra export corpus by name substring or entry address. It was made so a reverse-engineering session can pull one retail function into view without opening Ghidra or re-running analysis. Use it to read a native function before porting it, to list every method of a class, or to check a claim about retail behaviour against the decompiled code.
hp1-ghidra-export: A Ghidra headless post-script that decompiles every function of a program into one searchable C file plus a function table. It was written to turn the retail DLLs of a 2001 Unreal Engine 1 game into a grep-able corpus, so engine behaviour could be ported from the original code instead of reconstructed by experiment. Use it when a closed-source Windows binary needs whole-program search, when you want to find every caller or use of a constant across a DLL, or before porting native functions from an old game.
hp1-layout: Computes the in-memory member layout of a native engine class from a published C++ header and maps raw offsets to field names. It was built because decompiled code addresses fields as this+0x16c, and naming those offsets by hand is slow and error prone. Use it when reading decompiled Unreal Engine 1 code, when porting a native that touches actor fields, or to check that a header matches the binary.
hp1-run-test: Runs one level of the native game port unattended: it boots the map with audio muted, saves frames at chosen level times, quits on its own and keeps the log. It replaced window screenshots taken through the OS, which stopped working when the session lacked screen-recording permission. Use it to check a rendering or animation fix, to smoke-test every map for script errors, or to capture before and after images of a change.
hp1-upkg: A small inspector for Unreal Engine 1 package files (.u, .unr, .usa): header counts, an export listing filtered by name, and a dump of one export's state frame and tagged properties. It was written to debug saved games of a 2001 Unreal Engine 1 game, where a save written by a reimplemented engine failed to load and the bad property had to be found byte by byte. Use it to check what a map or save file stores for an actor, to compare a writer's output against what a loader expects, or to scan game content for which classes and textures a level uses.
hp1-utex: Exports the palette textures of an Unreal Engine 1 package (.utx, .u, .unr) as PNG files or as one labeled contact sheet, from the first mipmap and the texture's own palette. It was written to look at the portrait textures of a 2001 Unreal Engine 1 game, whose names and maps had to be checked by eye, after one-off decoders had been written twice for the same job. Use it to see what a texture package contains, to pull menu or HUD art for a comparison with a reimplementation, or to make a quick contact sheet of a whole package.
icon-render: A Swift command-line tool that asks macOS for the icon of a file or app bundle, the same way Finder and the Dock get it, and draws it into a PNG on a teal background. It was made while giving a game port's app bundle its original Windows icon, to confirm how macOS 26 frames a full-square legacy icon (it rounds the corners) without a person opening Finder. Use it after building or changing any .app icon, to compare an old icon with a new one, to check whether a transparent or odd-shaped icon gets a frame added by the system, or to make icon screenshots for docs.
icons.py: Makes the Switchboard KC web app's icons (192, 512, apple-touch 180, favicon 64, and a maskable 512 with the art in the middle 80 percent) from the iPhone app's 1024 master icon. It was made when the icon lost its 311 text, so one master file drives every size instead of hand-resizing each one. Use it after changing the Switchboard KC master icon, or as a pattern for deriving PWA icon sets from an iOS app icon.
ig: Read-only Instagram CLI that borrows the logged-in Chrome session to list an account's posts and scan tracked accounts into a JSON file, with pacing and a cooldown after a 429. Built to read event announcements from local Instagram accounts without an API, without ever posting, liking or following. Scanning local venues for events; checking cookie or cooldown status; reading recent posts from one account.
imessage-reader.py: Python reader for the local Messages chat.db that lists recent messages and searches, shows unread, and opens a chat by phone number or contact name. Built so Alex's texts can be queried from the command line and by skills without opening Messages. Checking who texted; finding what a person said; searching texts by keyword; scanning for unanswered messages in briefings.
imessage-send.py: Python script that sends an iMessage to a recipient with the given text through the Messages app. Built so MIST can send texts on Alex's behalf, with outbound messages always signed as his assistant. Sending a text to a contact from a routine or chat; delivering a reply or reminder by iMessage.
Inbox: Native window (pywebview) running a local Flask clone of Google Inbox over the Gmail API, with a one-tap Send to Things 3 that links back to the email. Built to recreate the discontinued Inbox by Gmail triage model and connect email straight to the Things 3 task list. Triaging Gmail; turning an email into a Things 3 task; working through the inbox with bundles and snoozes.
inbox-iphone-build-install: Shell script that generates the Xcode project, builds a signed Release build of the native Inbox SwiftUI Gmail client, and installs it on the paired iPhone via devicectl. Made because free-team provisioning expires every seven days and the app needed a repeatable one-command rebuild and reinstall. When the Inbox app stops launching on the phone; after changing the iOS source; refreshing the weekly signing with the phone unlocked and connected.
indeed.py (job-search Indeed lane): Discovery script that searches Indeed with a real Chrome in headless mode and gates the newest results for remote US seats and Kansas City local seats, employment type and listed pay. Built because Indeed blocks plain HTTP requests, and rewritten when its logged-out search stopped showing anything past page one. Daily job discovery on Indeed; checking a new keyword angle; finding Kansas City onsite IT postings.
ios-sideload-refresh: Python script that rebuilds and wirelessly reinstalls iOS sideloaded apps before their provisioning profiles expire, with status, discover and force modes. Expired profiles leave an app on the home screen that silently refuses to launch. Rebuilding early restarts the clock. Now run by hand since the paid developer plan lasts a year. Checking the expiry countdown with --status; refreshing sideloads before the yearly deadline; reinstalling a sideloaded app after a launch failure.
ironman: Python CLI reading the Ironman iPhone app's exercise-log JSON from a synced folder, printing week summaries and the running quest, or writing weekly vault notes. Built so the harness never has to parse the app's JSON itself. Checking this week's workout sets; projecting weeks into Obsidian; reading running quest level and next session.
itch-dl: Python script that lists and downloads files from free or pay-what-you-want itch.io pages by following the page's own download flow. Appears to have been built to fetch CC0 asset packs, such as character models, for animation and game projects. Downloading a free asset pack; filtering files by name; listing what an itch.io page offers before downloading.
itch-free-download: Downloads every file on a free or name-your-own-price itch.io page with a headless browser, by clicking through the 'no thanks, just take me to the downloads' step. Plain HTTP requests to the itch.io download endpoints redirect back to the store page, so a browser is necessary. It was made to get the Lurking Layers adaptive music pack for the table-conductor RPG audio player. Use it to get free game assets, music packs, sound effects or tools from itch.io without a manual browser session.
jackbox: CLI that plays Jackbox party games as a Claude player: launches a headless Chrome, joins rooms, runs an autopilot, and offers status, screenshots, DOM dumps and reports. Built so MIST can join Jackbox games with friends as a player through the browser without manual driving. Joining a Jackbox room; checking what phase the autopilot sees; reviewing a finished game log; stopping the autopilot.
jd-snapshot.py: Python script that loads a job posting in headless Chrome, opens its 'show more' sections and saves one full-page PNG into the listing's own vault folder, then records the image and a pay-range check on the listing note. It was made so that each qualifying job listing keeps a picture of the pay range as the employer posted it, for salary talks after the posting changes or is removed. Use it as the last step when a listing passes the job-search gates, to take a new dated image when a role is reposted, or as the pattern for any full-page archive image of a web page.
job-pipeline: A shareable job-search pipeline for Claude Code: board and ATS lanes, gates in code, a verb-level fit scorecard, one markdown note per posting, and fact-checked resume PDFs, with every personal value in one profile file. It was built to publish the harness job-search system so other people can clone and tune it. Use it to set up a job search for someone else, to compare against other job-search tools, or as the upstream when a harness lane changes.
jobspy_lane.py (job-search Glassdoor/Zip: Discovery script that searches Glassdoor and ZipRecruiter through the open-source JobSpy library and gates the rows for remote or Kansas City seats, full-time work and listed pay. Built because both sites block plain HTTP requests, so before this they reached the job scan only through alert emails. Daily job discovery on Glassdoor; pulling pay bands for a title; checking local Kansas City postings on aggregator sites.
kc-civic: Python CLI that reads Kansas City, Missouri public meeting schedules from the city's Legistar API and the EDC of Kansas City events feed, writes them to Google Calendar, and adds expected-meeting holds for bodies with a fixed cadence. For meetings with a published agenda it builds a packet of agenda and attachment text and runs a headless Claude that writes a prep note with public comment rules, the items worth a remark, research, and draft remarks. Its code subcommand downloads the city's Code of Ordinances and Zoning and Development Code from Municode into a local cache and searches it, which was added when a zoning question needed the exact use tables and the tenting ordinance. Use it to add a new city board to the calendar, to prep testimony for a specific meeting, to look up what a city ordinance or zoning use table actually says, or as a template for another city's Legistar instance.
kc-crash-geocoder: Places Kansas City crash records that name two streets but carry no coordinates at the point where both streets meet, using the city's street centerlines and OpenStreetMap freeway lines. It was built to map KCPD injury and fatal crashes against the city's safety projects and 311 traffic calming requests. Use it to geocode any KC dataset keyed by an on-street and at-street pair, to find crash hotspots, or to check a corridor's crash history before a petition or PIAC request.
kcmo-jobs: Reads every open posting on the City of Kansas City, Missouri job board (a PeopleSoft Candidate Gateway at psweb.kcmo.org) and the kcmo.gov executive careers page, using an off-screen Chrome, then gates IT and security titles against the onsite pay floor and diffs against yesterday. It was built because the city's NEOGOV page went empty while the real board held over a hundred jobs, and aggregator copies of city postings vanish without notice. Use it to check whether the city has an IT, security, or CISO opening, to run the city lane of the daily job scan, or as a model for scraping any other PeopleSoft Candidate Gateway employer board.
kcurbex: CLI for the KC Urbex forum that indexes site reports into an Obsidian folder and syncs board meetups to Google Calendar, run by a 12-hour watcher. Its sheet subcommand also imports a shared Google Sheet of urbex locations, geocodes each address, and writes the rows next to the forum reports. Built to track a gated urban exploration forum without manual checking, within what a Tier 1 account can see. Use it to refresh urbex reports in the vault, sync meetups to the calendar, import or re-pull a location spreadsheet, or check what the forum watcher last found.
kiwix-sync: A command that keeps the newest Kiwix ZIM dumps of English Wikipedia and the WikiProjectMed medical wiki on the external SSD. It reads the Kiwix mirror listing, downloads a new version with aria2c from the metalink, checks the full SHA-256, and only then deletes the old version. It was made to keep an offline reference library for use when the internet is not available, as the knowledge source for a local model on a Meshtastic mesh. Use it to add another offline book (Wiktionary, Stack Exchange, iFixit, Gutenberg), to check which dump version the disk holds, or as a pattern for any large verified download to a removable disk.
kqi: Shell launcher that runs the NIU KQi scooter Bluetooth script inside an app bundle so macOS attributes Bluetooth permission correctly, with commands like status, lock, and read. Bare Python from a terminal or Console is killed by TCC without a Bluetooth usage key. The bundle takes the grant once. Checking scooter battery; locking or unlocking it; reading or changing ride settings; logging in to the NIU cloud.
kqi-firmware-watch: A daily check of NIU's OTA update cloud for new KQi Air scooter firmware. It claims each of the five controllers' installed versions, downloads any newer image the server offers, and sends one alert. It was made because the motor, dashboard, battery and Bluetooth controllers had no published image to decompile, so the only cloud route is to catch a release when it appears. Use it to find out if NIU shipped a scooter update, to collect a firmware image for reverse engineering, or as a model for a watcher on a version-diff update endpoint.
lane-runlog: A run record for job-search lanes: it wraps any lane command, keeps one JSON line per run, and reports rows, survivors and leads per lane next to the tracker funnel by source. It was built because the daily scan left only a prose summary, so no one could tell which lanes produced applications. Use it to decide which lanes to keep, to tell a broken lane from a dry one, or to measure a new source.
launchd-table: Python script that prints the README's launchd table from plists git tracks, showing trigger, target script, loaded state, and purpose. Keeps the README table generated from real plists and script headers instead of hand-edited and stale. Regenerating the README launchd table; checking which jobs are loaded; fixing a purpose column at the script header.
league-scan: Python script that measures each fantasy manager's engagement from ESPN records: zero-score starters, bench points left, moves, and trade offer outcomes. Built to replace hand-kept league observations with computed numbers for the weekly routine and trade targeting. Weekly opponent modeling; choosing which manager to target with a trade offer; updating the playbook's league observations.
letter-pdf: Python script that renders a plain-markdown letter into a formal print-ready PDF with letterhead, headers, and running page footers in the house style. Appears to have been built so formal letters, such as to officials, come out consistently formatted without a word processor. Producing a printable letter; regenerating after edits; adding a running head to a multi-page letter.
limit-reset: Reads the Claude plan's limit resets (the grants behind Claude Code's /limit-reset command: 5-hour, weekly, full and Fable resets, each with a count and a use-by date) from the account usage endpoint, and redeems one through the same endpoint the CLI uses. It was built because the CLI only shows and spends these resets inside an interactive session, so unattended MIST runs hit the wall with an unused reset in hand and held resets expired unused. Use it to see what resets the account holds, to spend one when a routine or chat hits the plan limit (claude-api-gate and run-routine.sh call it before the API key), to use an anytime reset before it expires, or to check why a reset is not usable. The hourly launchd job com.exobrain.limit-reset runs the watch command and reports new, used and expiring resets.
lineup-precheck: Python pre-check that asks the lineup check for the starters' kickoffs and exits 3 when nothing locks in the next 27 hours. Built so the fantasy lineup routine stops before a model run starts on days with nothing to decide, which used to cost a full headless run to find out. Use it inside any launcher that should skip a routine when the next decision is far away, or as a template for cheap deterministic gates in front of model runs.
lineup-watch: Python watcher run every fifteen minutes that checks the fantasy lineup for problems before kickoff locks, notifies only on real issues, and with --fix repairs definite ones. Built so a missed OUT, bye or empty slot does not cost a week, without a banner on clean lineups. Checking lineup problems before a lock; debugging a missed alert; reviewing auto-fix behavior.
linkedin-mcp: Shell wrapper that launches mcp-server-linkedin with macOS hidden-target mode disabled so the browser runs in real headless mode. Built because hidden targets were destroyed when the startup window closed, which the server misread as an expired session and quarantined cookies. Starting the LinkedIn MCP server; diagnosing bogus sign-in prompts; patching the server after an update.
listings.py: Keeps the job-listing tracker folder in shape: every listing note lives in its own folder, and near-miss, skipped and unverified listings keep no note. It moves each near-miss note's full text into a JSONL ledger before it deletes the note, and the dedup, ATS watchlist, Workday and run-record scripts read that ledger, so dedup still works. Built when the tracker root held over 900 loose notes, most of them declined roles. Use it to clean up the listings folder after a scan, to bring back a declined listing that should be reconsidered, or to count how many roles were retired as near-misses.
loopkit: A Python engine for music that repeats with no seam. It renders additive-synthesis notes as Shepard stacks, one tone at every octave under a fixed bell curve, so a line can climb or fall forever, and it renders exactly one period with every note tail, the reverb, and the filters wrapped, so the file loops to the sample. Pitches can be pure 5-limit ratios, with a glide that pays back the comma so a just-tuned cycle still closes, and each render writes a one-period FLAC plus an MP3 with a loop window. It was built for a strange-loop piece that climbs through all 24 keys, after the piano engine could not do Shepard tones, pure tuning across a loop, or circular rendering. Use it for endlessly rising or falling music, ambient loops for an app or a game, Shepard-tone or just-intonation demonstrations, and sonifications of a mathematical structure.
lowes-stores: Builds the Lowe's store coordinate file for Penny Lane from an All the Places run: store number, city, state, zip, street address and GPS point for every US Lowe's. It was created when Lowe's removed the store sitemap the app read, which left the store locator with no distances. Use it to refresh Lowe's store locations after new stores open, to find the nearest Lowe's to a point, or as a pattern for pulling any chain's store list from All the Places.
luma: Python CLI for Luma events over the web app's private endpoints, using a browser session cookie: create, clone, update, cancel events and read guest lists. Built because Luma's free plan offers no official write API, and the Kansas City EA calendar needs events managed automatically. Creating or rescheduling a coffee or coworking event; checking RSVPs; cancelling an event.
luma-to-meetup: Python CLI mirroring future events from a Luma calendar onto a Meetup group as drafts, reporting drift when Luma events are cancelled. Built because Luma is where the events are authored but the group's members still watch Meetup. Syncing new events after creating them on Luma; publishing drafts; checking for cancelled events still live on Meetup.
lyricguard: A filter that masks lyric phrases in command output. It reads every song's lyrics from the animation kit's gitignored private folder and replaces any two consecutive lyric words with blocks, so copyrighted lyrics never reach a log, a terminal or a chat. It was built for a kinetic typography lyric video of a commercial song, where the lyrics had to be handled by scripts only. Use it to wrap any command that touches song lyrics, to scrub a log before reading it, or to test that a file holds no lyric text before a commit.
lyrics-align: Times every lyric word of a song to its isolated vocal stem and writes the timeline a lyric video page reads. It runs mist-vid's MMS_FA forced aligner one line at a time, repairs line boundaries where two lines claim the same words, adds held-note ends from the vocal level, song sections from repeated lines, hero words and function words, and writes a masked copy with placeholder words for layout review. It scores itself against vocal onsets, human LRC timings and an independent Whisper pass. Use it for kinetic typography, karaoke or word-synced captions of any song with known lyrics.
lyrics-fetch: Fetches a song's lyrics and line times from LRCLIB into the animation kit's gitignored private folder. It keeps the synced version that most matching records share and keeps the other synced versions as independent human timings, and it prints only counts and metadata. It was built for a lyric video of a commercial song and replaced a hand search of lyric sites. Use it to start any lyric video, karaoke or caption job for a released song, or to get human line timings to score an aligner against.
MapToGlobe: Local web app serving a production Vue build that wraps a flat equirectangular map onto a 3D globe with rings, moons, lighting, starfield, and JPG or GIF export. Appears to have been adopted to turn flat fictional or worldbuilding maps into rotating globes. Visualizing a homebrew world map as a planet; exporting a rotating GIF or screenshot; adding rings and moons to a planet.
marketplace: Curbside, a local web front end for Facebook Marketplace served from this Mac (shopping/bin/marketplace, port 5041), plus its watcher (marketplace watch, launchd every 30 minutes). It keeps a SQLite index of every listing near home by sweeping each category newest first in distance rings, gets exact distance from item-page pins, fingerprints photos to collapse reposts and flag photos shared across sellers, and sends saved-search alerts (new matches, price drops, cheaper relists) as one Discord and banner digest. It was built because the Facebook interface mixes in ads, shipped and out-of-area items, has weak filters and no real distance sort, and has no repost or price-drop memory. Use it to browse everything for sale near home by distance, to get alerted when a wanted item is listed or drops in price, to spot relisted or scam-photo listings, or as the data layer for other Marketplace analysis.
matter: A non-interactive wrapper around the matter.js controller shell that makes this computer a Matter admin on the home network. It was made to join smart lights that are already paired to a hub such as Google Home, so that settings the hub hides (for example the on/off transition time) can be written directly. Use it to pair a Matter device with a hub-issued pairing code, to read or write any cluster attribute, to send a cluster command, or to inspect a device the hub app does not show in detail.
mcp-call: A command-line client that calls any MCP server configured in the Claude config, by name. It lists a server's tools with their arguments, or calls one tool with key=value arguments and prints the result. It was built on 2026-10-07 because servers added during a session do not load until the next session, and a trip search needed them at once. Use it to call a newly added MCP server without restarting, to script MCP tools from shell pipelines or routines, or to debug what a server returns for a given call.
mcp-lazy: A stdio stub that takes the place of an MCP server in the Claude Code config and starts the actual server only when a session calls one of its tools. It answers the initialize handshake and the tool, prompt and resource lists from a cache, so the server name and tool names stay the same, and it stops the server again after a quiet period. It was made on 2026-10-12 after memory pressure alerts on an 8 GB Mac, where each open chat started twelve seldom used servers and spent approximately 600 MB on them. Use it to put a new stdio MCP server behind lazy start, to undo that for a server that must start with the session, to rebuild the cached tool lists after a server update, or to find why a wrapped server does not start.
meetup: Unofficial Python CLI for meetup.com that searches events, browses groups, reads event details, and RSVPs from the terminal. Built so event discovery and RSVPs for local meetups can be done by MIST without a browser session. Finding events near Kansas City; reading an event's details; RSVPing; scanning a group's upcoming events.
memory-index-check: A read-only lint for MIST's persistent memory index. It reads MEMORY.md and the index_<domain>.md sub-index files in the memory store and reports the index size against the loader's 24.4KB cap, over-long index lines, memory files that no index links to, and links to files that do not exist. It was written when the index went over the cap and 110 memory files turned out to have no index line at all, so no session could recall them. Run it after you add, rename, or delete a memory file, when the session-start hook prints a memory index WARN or FAIL, or before you prune the index to make room.
memory_eval.py: Held-out recall eval for the session-memory Zettelkasten: the zettels a later session updated are the ground truth, and each retrieval method is scored against the store as it stood before that session. Built to size the writer's candidate list and to test ranking ideas against real use instead of opinion. Use it after any change to the memory writer, recall ranking or tagging, or to compare BM25, embeddings and fusion on new data.
mesh-map: Builds a terrain map and line-of-sight table for a small LoRa radio mesh from a site list and a USGS 3DEP bare-earth elevation grid. It calculates terrain clearance and Fresnel margin for every pair of sites and writes an interactive MapLibre map (elevation tint, contours, links by result, profile per link, 3D terrain), a static PNG, profile charts and a JSON table. It was made for the friends' Meshtastic outage-comms plan, to replace one-off point-sample terrain checks. Use it to place a relay or window node, to check whether a new friend's address can join a mesh, to compare floors or roof mounts before buying hardware, or for any radio line-of-sight question in hilly terrain.
mfc: Command-line build for a public atlas of AI data centers in the US Midwest. It downloads a public data center dataset with satellite-based power and compute estimates, merges it with hand-researched project records, geocodes every site with a check that each point falls inside its own state, estimates compute from announced power, compares utilities' own load figures with the map, samples recent satellite images, and renders a static web page with every number filled in from the data. It was built to replace a one-off research answer with a map that can be refreshed in one command. Use it to refresh the atlas when new data lands, to check research records against the pages they quote, to place a site from a planning record's road corner, or as a pattern for any map built from a public dataset plus sourced research.
mid2mp3 / mp32mid: Pair of shell commands: mid2mp3 renders a MIDI file to MP3 or WAV with FluidSynth and a General MIDI soundfont; mp32mid transcribes audio to MIDI via Basic Pitch. Built to convert between MIDI and audio without opening a DAW, since VLC and other players do not handle MIDI well. Turning a .mid file into a playable MP3; transcribing a recording to MIDI; swapping the soundfont with MIDI_SOUNDFONT.
MIST Chess: Native desktop launcher for a chess training stack with Maia human-like opponents at nine rating levels, a full-strength engine, and a database GUI. Built to give Alex sparring partners that play like real people at a chosen rating, plus analysis, in one local repo. Playing a practice game at a target rating; analyzing a game with the strong engine; browsing the chess database.
MIST Console: Desktop app launcher that runs the MIST Console in-bundle Python (desktop.py), the chat window that hosts Claude sessions in the harness directory. Built as MIST's own desktop chat surface with routines, notifications, and model discovery, so sessions load the harness persona without a side-file. Opening a MIST chat; raising the console from a notification; relaunching the window after restarting the server.
MIST crystal animations: Node render pipeline for MIST's blue bipyramid crystal: 11 animation states in 7 looks, exported as transparent WebP, WebM and GIF, with sheet and strip previews. Built to give MIST a consistent, faceless animated visual identity that can be reused across the Console and videos. Adding a new state or mood for MIST; rendering a clip to overlay in a video; re-exporting the pack after editing animations.
MIST Radar: macOS warmer/colder phone finder that passively scans Bluetooth LE advertisements and shows signal strength in a window with a large MIST face. Built to find a misplaced phone by walking around with the laptop, without pairing or connecting to anything. Locating a lost phone in the apartment; checking whether a BLE device is nearby; debugging Bluetooth permission behavior.
MIST Studio: Local web app on port 5032 that generates songs with ACE-Step 1.5, plus stem splitting with demucs, lyric drafting via claude, and cover art via mist-image. Built as a local alternative to Suno-style song services, with swappable backends including a free Hugging Face Space, a rented GPU, and a mock. Making a full song from a prompt and lyrics; splitting a track into stems; generating cover art or lyrics for a track.
mist-alarm: Command-line client for the MIST Alarms hub that sets, lists and removes real alarms on Alex's iPhone. It posts to a Cloudflare Worker, which pushes the change to an AlarmKit app, and then waits for the phone to report that it holds the alarm. Built because no Mac-side tool could put an alarm on the phone, and a one-way send can fail silently. Use it to set a wake-up or reminder alarm from a chat, to schedule weekly alarms, to check which alarms the phone actually holds, or to feed a computed time (sleep-cycle calculator, calendar departure) into a real alarm.
mist-ask: Bash script that fires a notification with reply buttons whose taps post the chosen reply into the current Console chat as Alex's next message. Ensures decisions reach Alex as clickable banner buttons even when he is away from the window, instead of asking in text alone. Before a force push, delete, send, or anything hard to reverse; any decision needing a quick approve or deny; offering labeled choices.
mist-ask-mode: Shell script that fires a banner asking which permission mode to run in after a plan is approved, with buttons that set the mode and resume the chat. Built so approving a plan is separate from choosing how it is executed. Right after ExitPlanMode is approved in a Console chat; testing with MIST_ASK_DRYRUN=1.
mist-chatterbox-voice: A resident local text-to-speech service that speaks in MIST's cloned voice using Chatterbox Turbo on Apple's MLX framework, with the same /health and /say HTTP interface as the XTTS service. It was built as a faster, more natural engine than XTTS after a side-by-side test of local voice models, and it backs the Chatterbox button in the MIST Console voice pane. Use it when a script, app or briefing needs MIST's voice rendered close to real time, when comparing voice engines, or as the voice for a future phone or speaker integration.
mist-coach: Python script that archives the duel client's replay beside the newest duel log and prints the digest for review in the live session. Built for the /duel skill so post-game coaching reads a saved digest, with reasoning done in the session rather than a side call. After a Yu-Gi-Oh duel; reviewing a specific duel with --duel; tuning MIST's decks.
mist-confetti: Bash wrapper around a native confetti overlay that bursts across all displays with an optional victory tone. Built for explicit celebrations Alex asked to hear, so sound is on by default here though silent elsewhere. Celebrating a finished milestone; a visual-only burst with --silent; picking a shorter cue with --tone success.
mist-copilot: Launcher for MIST Copilot, a native SwiftUI menu-bar app that transcribes both sides of a call on-device and streams suggested answers into a floating overlay. Built as a local, private clone of commercial interview copilots such as ParakeetAI, keeping audio on the Mac. Starting the copilot before an interview or meeting; rebuilding the app bundle; checking the overlay hotkeys.
mist-duel: Bash launcher that starts the WindBot brain if needed and connects MIST to an EDOPro Yu-Gi-Oh room with a chosen deck. Built so MIST can be sat down at a duel with one command instead of manual bot setup. Starting a duel against MIST; picking another deck; rejoining after a stuck lobby.
mist-duel-cli: CLI giving MIST her seat in a Yu-Gi-Oh duel: waits for decisions from the brain, shows options with card text, and sends answers back. Built so duel choices are reasoned in a live Claude session instead of stateless calls. Playing EDOPro against MIST; reviewing recent decisions; recording how a duel ended.
mist-duel-preflight: Python script that checks everything required before MIST can duel in EDOPro and prints one line per check, exiting nonzero on failure. Built so a broken setup shows up by name instead of MIST silently playing as stock WindBot. Before starting a duel; diagnosing why MIST played scripted moves; after updating EDOPro or the brain service.
mist-duel-replay: Reads an EDOPro replay file with full information, showing both hands and set cards per phase, an event-per-line log, a summary, and decklists. Built so MIST can review games it played, see what was in each hand, and tune decks and coaching afterwards. Reviewing a finished duel; explaining a bot play; finding what the opponent held; tuning a deck after a loss.
mist-duel-review: Python CLI that turns a Yu-Gi-Oh duel log into a deterministic turn-by-turn digest, per-deck records, and a list of duels. Built so post-duel review reasons over observed board differences, not a reconstructed narrative, since MIST only sees her own seat. Reviewing a duel; checking a deck's win record; picking the latest log to tune decks or coach Alex.
mist-duel-roster: Python CLI that lists the decks MIST can play, filters by format, picks one avoiding the last played, and prints deck notes. Built so the duel skill stays deck-neutral and the roster lives in one place. Starting a duel; asking which decks are legal in a format; reading a deck's plan and watch-outs.
mist-eject: Shell wrapper around disk_eject.py that finds every process holding a busy external volume open, asks each one to quit the way it expects (launchd jobs are booted out and reloaded afterwards, app bundles get an AppleScript quit, the rest SIGTERM), then ejects. Built after a torrent daemon kept a media drive busy and macOS refused to eject while only naming a process ID. It never forces an unmount and never SIGKILLs; if a holder will not quit the volume stays mounted and the notification names it. Ejecting an external SSD that reports busy; previewing with --dry-run; releasing holders without ejecting with --no-eject.
mist-frame: Bash wrapper that wraps stdin as an UNTRUSTED data block with a shared preamble, for including third-party text in a model prompt. Built as a prompt-injection defense, so scripts in other directories can frame outside text without importing security internals. Any script passing chat messages, email or web text to a model; adding a new unattended runner; checking the preamble text.
mist-image: Python CLI generating an image from a text prompt on a cloud GPU via Cloudflare Workers AI or Pollinations, with reference-image support. Built so image generation never touches the Mac's limited RAM, and character looks stay consistent through reference images. Making any requested image; keeping a character consistent across poses; generating cover art.
mist-injection-scan: Bash wrapper around a stdlib Python scanner that flags instruction-shaped text in files loaded as context, exiting 1 on a hit. Built as a prompt-injection tripwire for context files, using Apple's Python so it works under launchd. Scanning a file before loading it as context; checking added lines in a diff; adding a scan step to a new pipeline.
mist-install: Python installer that copies MIST's executor DLL, decks and bot entries into EDOPro's WindBot, including bots.json entries generated from the roster. EDOPro updates overwrite the shipped bots.json and drop MIST from the dropdown, so this reinstalls idempotently. After updating EDOPro or ProjectIgnis; adding a deck to the roster; MIST missing from the bot list.
mist-launch: A ten-line Team-signed exec launcher plus a plist sweep. Every launchd job on the machine is declared as mist-launch followed by its original command, with AssociatedBundleIdentifiers naming MIST Console, so Login Items shows the fleet under the app instead of 90 rows called bash and python, and every job's file access is the launcher's Full Disk Access instead of a per-interpreter grant that broke on each Homebrew Python bump. Built 2026-10-12 after the audit of the memory watchdog found its notifier calls blocked by TCC. Use it when adding a launchd plist (declare through the launcher), when a job hits Operation not permitted under launchd, or when a new project repo's plists need re-declaring.
mist-music: Shell shim that runs the MIST music CLI in its virtual environment to render sheet music, transcribe audio to notation, and generate songs. Built to bring music generation and notation conversion into one command, with music21 and oemer dependencies in a dedicated venv. Turning MIDI or MusicXML into audio; transcribing a recording; generating a song when Alex asks for one.
mist-notify: Bash tool that shows a clickable macOS notification with sound, an Open-link button for its source, image, reply and action buttons, and logs it to the Console's history. Built so every alert from watchers and MIST lands in one history and, when tapped, in a MIST Console chat: the chat that sent it, or a new chat seeded with the notification text, the sender's context and the line Alex wants to chat about this. Alerting Alex when a watcher fires; sending a briefing or triage banner; offering reply or action buttons; handing a headless routine's result to a chat Alex can continue.
mist-og: Python CLI that publishes one small Open Graph HTML page per image on GitHub Pages so an image renders as a link card in places that block photo uploads. Built for Facebook comment boxes that reject attachments but render link previews from og:image, with content-hashed filenames to defeat stale caches. Posting an image where attachments are blocked; adding or updating a card; sharing an image as a link preview.
mist-progress: CLI that draws a live, in-place updating progress bar in the MIST Console chat, either by wrapping a command and parsing its progress output or by taking values you compute. Built so long downloads, uploads, installs, and clones show visible progress in the chat instead of leaving Alex staring at a silent terminal. Wrap any command that takes more than a few seconds, such as a model download, clone, or install; report progress for a loop you measure yourself with start, set, and done.
mist-say: Bash CLI that speaks text in MIST's cloned voice through the resident service or a cold-start fallback, with a global mute switch. Built to give MIST an offline voice for spoken briefings and alerts. Speaking a short message; rendering audio to a file; muting all playback.
mist-studio: Bash launcher starting the MIST Studio song-generation server on port 5032 under the project's venv, with an option to open the browser. Provides the command-line entry to the local Suno-style studio built on ACE-Step 1.5. Starting the studio server manually; opening it in the browser; running it on another port.
mist-tcc-carry: Shell wrapper running a Python script under a dedicated interpreter that re-points the Claude CLI's macOS TCC grants to the path of its latest auto-update. Built because each Claude CLI update moves its binary and strands its permissions, and Full Disk Access needs a private interpreter to read TCC.db. After a Claude CLI update breaks permissions; checking pending grants with --check; pruning old versions with --prune.
mist-vid: GPU compositor that cuts a music video from a movie's footage: a YAML edit anchored to song bars, beats and lyric lines renders through OpenGL shaders (LUT grades, bloom, film grain, gl-transitions with a paper page curl, RIFE slow motion, gold-leaf and ink titles, paper cards, light leaks, double exposures) to ffmpeg, with an audio mixer that levels film dialogue and ducks the song under it. Built for a Princess Bride fan music video, after mist-ytp proved too crude for a cinematic, beat-synced edit with designed typography. Also bundles the analysis side: shot detection and contact sheets for catalog agents, catalog queries, filmstrips, whisper word timings, beat and downbeat grids, song-in-film alignment, and review sheets. Use it to make a music video or trailer from a movie or show, to cut footage on the beat of a song, to add storybook titles and page-turn transitions to a video, or to render slow-motion shots with frame interpolation.
mist-ytp: Script-driven YouTube Poop renderer that cuts clips, mixes sentences and applies effects, running under the project venv with Whisper transcription. Appears to have been built to make YouTube Poop style edits from a script rather than by hand in a video editor. Making a YTP from source clips; remixing sentences from a transcript; rendering a scripted edit.
monthly-climate-history: uv script that charts a month's long-run climate history for a US county, using NOAA nClimGrid for temperature and ERA5 for dewpoint and humidity, with trend lines and confidence bands. Appears to have been built to answer whether a given month has gotten warmer or more humid over a century, with stated trend uncertainty and no venv setup. Answering climate trend questions for Kansas City or another county; making light and dark charts for a note or post; checking whether a trend is detectable.
moreboards.py (job-search multi-board la: Discovery script that reads thirteen job boards with public JSON or RSS paths (SimplyHired, SmartRecruiters, Workable, ClearanceJobs, Working Nomads, Jobicy, RemoteOK, three Kansas City employer career APIs, Oracle Health, HigherEdJobs, Hacker News Who is hiring) and runs every row through one title, location, employment-type and pay gate. Built to widen the job scan beyond LinkedIn and the earlier lanes after a scouting pass found these data paths open to curl. Daily job discovery; adding another board that has a JSON search endpoint; checking Kansas City employers for onsite IT seats; finding remote analyst postings with listed pay.
mp: Command-line tool for public missing-person searches that lists cases, checks NCIC and NamUs status, ranks unidentified-person candidates, sweeps news, and scans terrain, with a change-only notify mode. Built to help a public missing-person search by combining read-only public sources into one repeatable scan, with case files kept outside the repo. Running a scan on a case; watching for changes with mp watch; checking source conflicts between databases.
mp (missing-person toolkit): Public CLI for assisting a missing-person search: case status across NamUs and state feeds, unidentified-person candidate ranking, newsroom watching, and terrain mapping for ground searches. Built while helping with a real search, with the case as a config file so it generalizes to any US case. Private case data stays in the vault, not the repo. Checking a case's database status; ranking unidentified-person candidates; watching news for a case; mapping terrain around a last-seen point.
mp-rate: Python script reporting how often the missing-person watcher's news-candidate track fires, read from timestamps in case history. Built to test empirically whether the two-agreement promotion threshold is right, since it was set from one cold-start sample. Reviewing the steady-state candidate rate; deciding whether to change the threshold; checking watcher output volume.
musictheory-2008: Local mirror of musictheory.net as of December 2008, rebuilt from the Internet Archive, with Flash trainers running through vendored Ruffle WASM on port 8008. Built to preserve and run the old Flash music theory trainers that no longer work on the live site. Starting the server to use the old ear and note trainers; extending the mirror with more archived pages; checking why a trainer fails (must be served, not file://).
mychart: A command line for every Epic MyChart patient portal account. It signs in with a passkey kept in the macOS Keychain, copies about thirty chart categories (labs, medications, visits, messages, bills, imaging, documents) into a local SQLite store, finds what changed, and can send one digest of new items. It also has a SMART on FHIR lane for coded data and an importer for a Cures Act EHI export. It was built to replace a hosted MyChart connector that kept credentials on a third-party server and worked only inside a chat. Use it to read or trend lab results across health systems, to see what is new after a visit, to download a document or a statement, or to add a new health system's portal.
mychart-engine: A maintenance script for the OpenRecord engine that the mychart command line drives. It clones the source-available repository, checks out the commit pinned in mychart/ENGINE_PIN, builds it with Bun, and on update it smoke-tests the new build against the public fake MyChart before it moves the pin. It exists because the engine cannot be vendored or redistributed and the npm release lags the repository. Use it after a fresh restore, when a MyChart sync breaks after a portal change, or to pick up new engine capabilities.
mychart-mcp: A local stdio MCP server over the same MyChart accounts and store as the mychart command line. It gives a chat thirteen tools: read a category, list changes, trend a lab value, search, run any read capability live, sync, and send a message to a care team only after a prepare step and an explicit confirm. Every result with chart text comes back framed as untrusted data. It was built to replace the hosted claude.ai MyChart connector. Use it when a conversation needs lab results, appointments, care-team messages, bills, or clinical notes.
mykcmo-mcp: Launcher for the myKCMO MCP server, which reads Kansas City 311 service requests from open data and can file confirm-gated reports. Built to expose city 311 data and reporting to Claude through stdio, reading optional settings from the harness environment. Looking up nearby 311 requests; checking city response stats; filing a 311 report after confirming; re-registering the MCP server.
mykcmo-refresh-key: Downloads the newest Android build of the Kansas City 311 app, decompiles the classes that hold its API signing key, city id, and app version, proves them with one signed read, and writes them to a gitignored config file. It exists because the 311 MCP server and the KC 311 iPhone app talk to the city app's private backend, and the vendor can rotate that key in any app update. Use it when 311 calls fail with a signature error, when the MCP server says the key was rejected, after a city app update, or to check the key with --check.
narrate.py: Python script that reads a Markdown note or piped text aloud in Alex's cloned MIST voice and saves an MP3, using the local voice server. Built to turn briefings and notes into audio in MIST's voice, pre-rendered because the local model is slower than real time. Making an audio morning briefing or evening winddown; narrating a news briefing podcast; converting any note to an MP3 with serve.py running.
net-gate: A wrapper that a launchd watcher runs in front of its real command. It probes the network first, and during an outage it skips the run, exits cleanly, and records the skip in one shared state file. It was made after a DNS outage made seven watchers fail one by one and only one of them gave an alert, which looked like a bug in that watcher. It sends one alert per outage that lasts more than ten minutes, with a check of each DNS server, and one recovery note, and it then reruns every job that was skipped. Use it for any new launchd job that needs the internet, to find out why watchers went quiet, or to diagnose which DNS server failed.
nextdns: A command-line client for the NextDNS API that reads the harness .env for the key and a default profile. It relinks the home network's public IP to a profile, prints the profile's status and the newest query, pulls the query log and per-domain tallies, and edits the denylist, allowlist, native tracking protection and blocklists, with a raw config patch for anything else. It was built for the TV Debloat and Privacy project, so the Samsung TV's DNS could run through a log-only NextDNS profile and then get the Samsung telemetry domains blocked, replacing hand-made curl calls. Use it to check what a device phones home to, to keep a linked IP current from a launchd job, to push a domain list into a NextDNS denylist, or to audit the Mac's own DNS traffic.
Night Watch: Local desktop app showing a Kansas City neighborhood safety feed: KC open crime data plus real-time National Weather Service alerts, on a map. Built because no clean, legal, real-time, geocoded nearby-incident feed exists; it combines lagged official data with live weather alerts. Checking severe weather or recent nearby incidents; opening the map GUI; reviewing the weekly crime digest for the home area.
NIU KQi: App bundle that runs the kqi_ble.py Bluetooth script from the niu-kqi project so macOS attributes Bluetooth permission to this bundle, capturing output and exit code to log files. Built because BLE access from a script needs a bundle with its own TCC identity to talk to the NIU KQi scooter. Any scooter command over Bluetooth such as battery or lock; when a BLE call from a terminal is blocked by permissions.
nudge-watch: A watcher that reads another fantasy team's lineup and drafts one short DM to that manager when a rule about a fixable lineup hole holds, such as a starter whose team does not play or a weaker starter over a better bench player. It was built so a lineup tip to a rival's opponent goes out only while it is still true, instead of a hand-written message that can go stale before anyone sends it. Each draft reaches the owner as a Send, Rewrite or Skip banner through chat-draft, and is withdrawn if the other manager fixes the lineup first. Use it to help the opponent of a bye-race rival, to queue any conditional DM that depends on a lineup, or as the pattern for a watcher that drafts but never sends.
ocr_book.py (Turn To): Reads a scanned book PDF page by page with Apple's on-device LiveText OCR and saves every line (or every word) with its position as JSON. It was built to pull the 400 numbered sections out of a Fighting Fantasy gamebook scan whose own Internet Archive text layer was too poor to use. Use it to get clean text from any scanned book or rulebook, to locate words on a page image for clickable overlays, or to compare two scans of one book.
Open in Google Calendar (.ics handler): Installer that builds a macOS app registered as the default .ics handler, parsing invites itself and opening them as pre-filled Google Calendar pages. Built so calendar invites open in Google Calendar rather than Apple Calendar, which is where Alex's schedule lives. Reinstalling the handler on a new Mac; debugging an invite that opens wrong; checking how many events open as create pages versus import.
opfp-sync: Pulls the upstream One Pace for Plex metadata repo (episode NFOs, season and exception maps, the rename script) and deploys it into the Plex show folder where the rename step actually runs. Built because the clone sat unfetched for months and new releases kept their raw release names since no NFO existed for them. Use it when new One Pace episodes show up unnamed in Plex, when upstream adds an arc, or to force a metadata refresh after a manual clone change.
orrery: Command-line tool and local editor server for The Great Wheel, a public 3D map of the D&D multiverse (Spelljammer crystal spheres and the phlogiston so far). It pulls GitHub edits at start, serves the map with an edit mode, joins the public atlas with a private overlay of DM notes and secret items and splits them again on save, checks the atlas, and commits and pushes the public repo (GitHub Pages rebuilds the site) and the private overlay repo. It was built so that spheres, currents and bodies can be added through forms instead of hand-edited JSON, without GitHub edits and local edits overwriting each other. Use it to add a sphere, a current or a body, to check the atlas after a hand edit, or to publish a map change.
orrery-models: A headless Blender pipeline that turns downloaded source models into small GLB files for the web: it reduces triangle counts, centers and scales each model, shrinks textures, bakes ambient occlusion into vertex colors, and composes scenes from kit pieces. It was built to give The Great Wheel map real models (photoscanned asteroids, an anatomical skull, a castle on floating land, an asteroid city) in place of placeholder shapes, at about 1.7 MB for all of them. Use it when a web 3D scene needs a heavy scan or a Poly Haven asset cut down to a web budget, when several CC0 kit pieces must become one model, or when a model needs baked shadows without a texture.
paperclip-meme: Shell launcher that serves the paperclip meme generator on localhost port 5031 and opens it, served rather than file:// so PNG export works. Built because fetch and canvas export are blocked on file origins, which the Clippy image export needs. Opening the meme generator from a terminal; exporting a Clippy meme PNG; changing PORT.
Passage: Local Flask paywall-remover app on port 5015 that races independent bypass methods (archives, crawler spoof, page JSON, feeds, a headless browser) and keeps the best result, plus a paper lane that turns a DOI, PMID or arXiv id into the paper's PDF from open-access copies first and then Sci-Hub, LibGen and Anna's Archive. Built as a durable synthesis of paywall-bypass techniques instead of one trick that stops working; it logs every rail attempt and has a benchmark command that measures pass rates on a fresh corpus. Use it to read a paywalled article, to get the PDF of a journal paper from a DOI, or to measure which bypass methods still work on a site.
pe-triage: uv script that statically triages a Windows PE file, reporting headers, sections, imports, resources, overlay, packer tells, entropy, and hashes without executing it. Appears to have been built for safely inspecting suspicious Windows executables before deciding whether to trust or analyze them further. Looking at an unknown installer or download; getting hashes to look up; deciding whether deeper Ghidra analysis is warranted.
penny-lane: Penny Lane finds retail 'penny items' (register price $0.01, the chain's pull-from-floor signal) and near-penny clearance at specific stores. It pulls community penny lists (PennyCentral, PennyRecon, Freebie Guy, RetailShout, RebelDealz), checks every reported SKU/UPC live at the user's Home Depot, Dollar General, Lowe's and Walmart stores for price, clearance state and on-shelf quantity, sweeps Home Depot's in-store Special Values nightly, and scores each item-store pair 0-100 with reasons. Built because the viral penny-deal videos show what a reporter found elsewhere, not whether it is still on the shelf nearby. Use it to: check a barcode in a store from the iPhone app, see which reported pennies are stocked at a given store, watch an item's markdown cadence, or get a notification when something nearby reaches the penny stage.
pianokit: Python engine that plays a piano score written as code. It voices the chords and runs the left-hand patterns, then adds rubato, pedal, dynamics, and small timing variation. Output is an MP3 on a sampled grand piano in a synthesized hall, plus performance and score MIDI files, in equal temperament or in adaptive just intonation that retunes each chord to pure ratios. Built when Alex asked for a piano piece composed in Python, because the existing mid2mp3 path plays written notes exactly as written, on a small General MIDI piano. Use it to write another piano piece, re-render one at a new tempo, key, reverb level, or tuning, compare equal temperament with just intonation, or check that a melody stands out over its accompaniment.
pin-python3-default: Shell script that points the Homebrew python3, pip3 and python3-config names at the Python version that holds the harness packages, and prints a line when it changes them. It was made after a new Homebrew dependency installed a newer Python that took over the python3 name, which broke every script that imports third-party packages. Run it when python3 reports an unexpected version, after a Homebrew upgrade that adds a new Python, or when the harness moves to a newer Python on purpose.
Plainsong: Hemingway-style readability tool served as a local web page on port 5020, highlighting dense sentences, passive voice, adverbs, qualifiers, and complex words. Built as a clean-room reimplementation of the Hemingway Editor that also catches irregular passive participles the original misses. Checking a draft for readability before sending or publishing; tuning prose to a lower grade level; spotting passive constructions.
plaud-fetch.py: A script that downloads the speaker-named transcript of every Plaud recording from the Plaud cloud and saves each one as a JSON file. It was made because the Google Drive auto-export is written once when a recording finishes, so speaker names that Plaud assigns later by voice print or manual rename never reach Drive. Use it before counting or extracting a person's own speech from recordings, to refresh names after speakers are renamed in the Plaud app, or to get timestamped, speaker-attributed segments for analysis.
plex-reencode: A command that converts oversized videos in a Plex media library to HEVC, one file at a time. It uses ab-av1 to find the lowest quality setting that keeps a sampled VMAF target, encodes with the Apple hardware encoder, then runs a full-length VMAF pass and stream and duration checks before one rename replaces the original. It was made when the external media drive was 98% full and the offline Wikipedia update needed approximately 120 GiB, so space had to come back without deleting titles. Use it to free space on a media drive, to find which files in a library are encoded inefficiently, or as a pattern for any batch file conversion that must not lose an original before the new file is verified.
Pocket Dungeon: Local desktop and web app for running the Pocket Dungeon 2.0 solo dungeon-crawl game, automating dice, room generation, combat math and treasure tables. Appears to have been built to remove the bookkeeping from the paper game while leaving map and tactical choices to the player. Playing a solo dungeon crawl; generating rooms and treasure; resolving combat quickly.
pogo: Command-line client for Pokemon Go community data and for Alex's own account files. Live lanes: events, raid bosses, field research, egg pools, Team GO Rocket lineups and promo codes from LeekDuck's hourly scrape; the Pokedex (stats, moves, evolutions, megas, shiny status, type matchups) from pogoapi.net; PvPoke league and cup rankings; CP and IV calculators. Account lanes: import a Poke Genie or Calcy IV box-scan CSV (box list/stats/dupes/diff) and the official Niantic data-request zip (account show/activity/spend), and an inbox watcher that ingests either file from iCloud Drive/Pokemon GO or Downloads. Built when a Pokemon Go MCP/CLI was requested and no CLI existed; it is the scriptable twin of the pokemon-go MCP server. Use it for what is in raids or eggs right now, when the next Community Day is, what a Pokemon is weak to, where it ranks in Great League, which of Alex's own Pokemon to keep or transfer, or what his account export says. Every lane has --json.
