pokemon-go-mcp: Launcher for the Pokemon Go MCP server, a fork of GhostTypes/pokemon-go-mcp that exposes 43 read-only tools over LeekDuck's Pokemon Go data: current and upcoming events, raid bosses by tier, field research and rewards, egg pools, Team GO Rocket lineups with type weaknesses, promo codes and a daily-priorities digest. Adopted instead of writing a server from scratch; the fork adds a live fetch of the hourly data branch with a disk cache so the tools stop serving a stale snapshot. Registered as pokemon-go in the harness .mcp.json; use it whenever a chat needs Pokemon Go event, raid or research answers as tools rather than shelling out to the pogo CLI.
Pomodoro: Native macOS pomodoro timer in Things 3 styling, built with pywebview, that logs completed sessions into Obsidian daily notes. Built to time focused work and record it in the vault automatically instead of tracking sessions by hand. Starting a focus block; reviewing how many sessions were logged in a day; extending the timer's logging.
portal-accept: Gets a laptop through a Wi-Fi captive portal without the system's mini browser. It opens the portal in headless Chromium, ticks the checkboxes, fills named fields, clicks the accept or connect button, and repeats until Apple's probe page answers. It keeps a screenshot and the HTML of every page. Built for a cinema guest network whose confirm button did nothing in the phone's portal sheet, at a moment when no assistant was reachable. Use it for hotel, airport, cafe or venue Wi-Fi that will not let you on, or to record what a portal does for later analysis.
posting-liveness: Checks whether job postings are still open by asking the ATS API first (Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters, Ashby, Workday) and falling back to the page text. It replaced browser loads and manual checks for stale listings, and its first sweep closed 45 dead tracker notes. Use it before building application documents, to clean the tracker, or to verify any posting URL someone sends.
priory: CLI for The Priory, a self-hosted deterministic news aggregator with bias bars and blindspot detection, providing status, ingest, feed loading, the web server, and embedding warmup. Built as a Ground News and Base Rate Times style aggregator forked from MuckScraper, keeping ingest, clustering, and bias math free of LLM calls. Checking pipeline health; loading feeds or forcing an ingest; starting the web UI on port 5025; warming embeddings after a restart.
procname: Builds a small binary per Python daemon so the process shows its own name in Activity Monitor and Stats instead of a generic Python or python3.X row. It loads the target interpreter's libpython in-process and keeps sys.executable, sys.prefix and sys.path identical to that interpreter, so venvs behave the same, and it falls back to the plain interpreter if libpython disappears. It was created after a memory-pressure check on the 8 GB Mac showed many unnamed Python rows that could not be told apart without a terminal. Use it when a new launchd Python daemon or stdio MCP server is added, when Stats shows an anonymous Python process, or after a Python upgrade to verify or rebuild the existing shims.
ps5-autopilot: Reflex loop that lets MIST play a split-screen shooter through the ps5-session link. About eight times a second it reads player 1's half of the frame, holds the trigger while the reticle is red, steers toward red radar blips and dark figures on the screen, levels the camera when it sees too much sky, jumps when stuck, and taps through the respawn menus. Built so MIST could be a real teammate in Star Wars Battlefront, where a model turn is far too slow to aim. Use it as the starting point for any game MIST plays on the PS5, or retune its color thresholds for another map or game.
ps5-pair: Pairs this Mac with the household PS5 for Remote Play through pyremoteplay, with every input passed as an argument instead of an interactive prompt. Built so a chat session can complete the PSN sign-in and the Link Device PIN step without a terminal, which the library's own CLI requires. Use it to register a new PSN account with the console, to re-pair after a console reset, or to check which accounts are registered.
ps5-session: Long-running PS5 Remote Play link. It keeps one session open through pyremoteplay, writes the latest decoded frame to a JPEG twice a second, and takes controller commands over a UNIX socket, so a MIST session can see the TV and press buttons. Built the night Alex asked to play split-screen Battlefront with MIST, because the ten-second smoke test could not hold a game. Use it to play any PS5 game as a second player, to watch what the console shows, or to automate menu navigation on the console.
ps5-smoke: Smoke test for the PS5 Remote Play link: streams video for a few seconds, counts decoded frames, saves sample PNGs, and taps a button part way through so the saved frames prove both directions work. Built as the first check after pairing and as the regression test for an unmaintained protocol library against new console firmware. Use it when a Remote Play session will not start, after a PS5 system update, or to grab a quick screenshot of what the console is showing.
ps5ctl: Command-line client for the ps5-session daemon. Sends one command line to the live Remote Play link and prints the reply, so a chat session can press buttons, move the sticks, wait, and grab a screenshot of the PS5 in a single shell call. Built alongside ps5-session so MIST can play Battlefront as player 2 with ordinary tool calls. Use it to drive a game, step through console menus, or capture what the PS5 is showing.
ps5read: Reads the words on the PS5 screen with Apple's on-device text recognition. It grabs a fresh frame from the ps5-session daemon (or any saved image), recognizes text in the whole screen or one split-screen half, and prints each line with its position. Built so MIST can read game menus, dialogue options and tooltips cheaply while playing BG3 split screen, instead of looking at a full screenshot every time. Use it to check which menu item is highlighted, read dialogue choices, find a button prompt, or OCR any screenshot on the Mac.
push-rom: Python CLI that pushes game files over SSH to an Anbernic RG35XX handheld, inferring the system folder from the extension and verifying with a remote sha256. The stock OS has no file transfer, so this drives the community SSH app to make adding games repeatable. Adding a game or disc image to the handheld; listing system folders; first-time setup with the device IP.
quest-verify: Python script that matches phone-recorded quest attempts against Fitbit activity by time, stamps verification on each, and rewrites the exercise log. Made so run quests in the ironman app are confirmed by watch data rather than self-reported, and unmatched watch runs are added. After a run to verify attempts; backfilling with --days; previewing with --dry-run; emitting JSON events for a watcher.
ramon: Python CLI that books haircuts at Salon Ramon from the terminal through the salon's booking system. Built to book the recurring haircut without using the salon's website. Booking or rebooking a haircut; checking open slots; the six-week haircut reminder.
Rasterbator: App launcher that serves the local posterizer project on port 5021 with python http.server and opens it in the browser. Appears to be a local rasterbator-style tool that splits an image into printable poster pages, opened as an app. Turning an image into a multi-page poster for printing; reopening the tool without a terminal.
rea: Open-source reverse engineering toolkit that runs as a CLI and an MCP server. It decompiles native binaries through Ghidra, and statically inspects JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, Mach-O and PE files, APKs, firmware, plists, HAR captures and websites, with evidence for each result. It was adopted to give agent sessions one structured interface for decompiling and analysis work, in place of hand-driven analyzeHeadless scripts. Use it to decompile a function in an unknown binary, to find how a feature in a closed-source Mac or Electron app works, to compare two versions of an app, or to inspect an APK or .NET assembly before reconstruction.
rea-update: Bash script that compares the installed rea reverse engineering CLI with the newest npm release and, when npm is ahead, updates it, re-runs its Claude Code setup, pins the Homebrew provider paths, wraps the MCP server in mcp-lazy again and restores the local block in the reverse-engineer-anything skill. It was built so the reverse engineering skill always starts on the current release, because rea ships fixes often and a bare setup run undoes the local MCP and skill changes. Use it before any decompiling or binary analysis task, after a rea MCP tool fails in a way an upstream fix can explain, or to repair the rea registration after someone ran rea setup by hand.
reddit-search: Keyword search over a subreddit's archive, read from the Arctic Shift archive API with no Reddit credentials, with the comment trees of the most-discussed hits. It was made when a research pass could not read Reddit at all: the .json endpoints, old.reddit and RSS are blocked, so subagents reported zero threads. Use it for 'what does r/<sub> say about X' questions: local restaurant and cafe opinions, product experiences, neighborhood questions, fanfic recommendation threads, any thread hunt that needs the comments and not only the titles. On large subreddits use --title, because full-text search times out there. Output is one JSON file in reddit/data plus a ranked summary on stdout.
render_dice.py: Renders photoreal traditional white six-sided dice in Blender, one transparent PNG per face and turn, each with a soft contact shadow. It was made for the Turn To gamebook reader after the printed line-art dice looked flat, because no CC0 photoreal dice model existed on Poly Haven. Use it to get dice images for any game UI, app icon or video, or as a starting point for rendering other small product-style objects on a transparent background.
Rental Harmony: Offline AppleScript-wrapped web app that divides rent fairly among roommates using the Sperner's Lemma method from Francis Su's paper, cloning the NYT calculator. Built because the original New York Times calculator will eventually be deprecated and the underlying math is worth preserving as a local tool. Splitting rent for a new or changing household; comparing room preferences fairly; demonstrating envy-free division.
repo-offload: Removes a local git clone whose work is already on its GitHub remote, after saving any local-only branches and stashes as a git bundle and recording the repo in a markdown ledger. Built for the 2026-10 disk cleanup, where dozens of finished project clones sat in Documents with their venvs and build output; before it, offloading meant checking push state by hand per repo. Use it to free space by dropping stale clones, to retire a finished project without losing its local branches, or to clear Documents before a machine migration.
restart-server: Bash script that restarts the detached MIST Console server holding port 5014 and reopens the app, guarded against repeat runs. Needed because edits to the server Python code never reload by relaunching the window, since the server is an orphaned process. After editing app.py, bridge.py, or share.py; run detached, not inline from a console chat; when the console serves stale code.
restart-server-when-idle: Bash script that waits until no Console chat transcript changed and there was no keyboard or mouse input for a set time, then restarts the MIST Console server. Backend edits sometimes land while other chats are mid-turn, and an immediate restart would cut them off. Deploying Console backend changes safely; restarting during active chats; running detached through launchctl submit.
resume-factcheck: Checks a tailored resume or cover letter against the canonical resume data and the job description, and stops a build on any figure that neither source supports. It was added after a review of other job tools showed none of the harness checked its own output for invented claims. Use it before sending any application document, when tailoring to a new JD, or to audit old letters for unsupported numbers.
ringer_board: Python script that extracts The Ringer's preseason fantasy football rankings from the page's embedded Next.js data, including positional rank, auction value, bye, and per-expert ranks. Their published Google Sheet is half-PPR and stale, so this pulls the live full-PPR board directly for draft preparation. Re-running before draft day; comparing formats (PPR, half, superflex, dynasty); feeding ranks into the VOR board build.
rival-scan: Read-only CLI that reads the other teams in Alex's ESPN fantasy league from the league's own record: each team's uncovered lineup needs this week and next, adds, K and D/ST streams, waiver claims won and lost, when each manager acts and was last seen, the players on waivers with this league's measured claim rates, the week's opponent, the bye race, and the trade market. It was built so that every fantasy routine, the daily briefing and the Scorebug app's WIRE tab see rival behavior, after a free agent we had flagged went to a rival the next morning. Use it before a waiver claim to see who else needs the position and whether a claim from last priority can land, before a lineup call to read the opponent's holes, to score waiver predictions after each run, or to watch the veto window on a trade between two other teams.
roster-news: Python script printing the last day or two of player-specific news for the fantasy roster, optionally the watch list, as markdown. ESPN attaches league-wide roundups to every feed, so this filters to headlines naming the player and feeds the daily briefing. Adding roster news to the briefing; widening the window with --hours or --all; including the watch list with --watch.
roster-watch: Python CLI behind the roster-watch launchd job that diffs fantasy roster status against the last run, banners Alex, and hands judgment cases to a routine. Built to notice injuries, claims and trade offers between scheduled runs, including bench-for-wire swap opportunities. Running a manual check with --dry-run or --no-routine; testing watcher logic; reviewing the incident log.
routine-guard: Shell shim that runs a Console routine only when today's weekday is in a given list, otherwise logs a skip and exits. Created after a Monday evening run fired the Tuesday routine because the wrapper checked time of day but not the weekday. Scheduling a weekday-specific launchd routine; debugging a routine that fired on the wrong day.
routine-log: Bash helper that appends one timestamped line to the fantasy routine log. Built so routine runs that decide nothing record that they ran without adding lines to the playbook's Season log, which had grown with 'no changes' entries. Use it from any headless routine for a no-op record, or tail the log to see what the routines did between decisions.
sab-build-modules: Python script on the android branch of bible-study that converts scraped Skeptic's Annotated Bible JSON into SWORD modules (KJV text, commentary, general book) using osis2mod and xml2gbs. Built for the AndBible fork so the annotated Bible loads on first launch, since the iOS app has no SWORD reader. Regenerating modules after the scraped data changes; a quick partial build with --books or --osis-only; debugging module content in the Android app.
SailboatRetro: Local web app on port 5175 for TTRPG session retrospectives using the sailboat metaphor of wind, anchor, rocks and island. Built to structure debriefs after tabletop campaign sessions and keep the results with campaign notes. After a D&D or other TTRPG session; comparing what went well against risks across sessions; planning the next session.
salon-ramon: CLI that lists open slots, books, views and cancels haircut appointments at Salon Ramon through its scheduling software, dry-run unless confirmed, with a 6-week cadence helper. Replaced the earlier Booksy-based booking tool in September 2026 when Alex's stylist moved to this booking system. Finding the next haircut slot; booking or cancelling an appointment; the daily haircut-check job deciding whether one is due.
scan-verse: Command-line scansion checker for song lyrics and verse. It reads a lyric in markdown, skips headings, singer labels and stage directions, and reports per stanza the syllable count of each line, the rhyme scheme and a meter guess from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary, then flags lines far from the stanza's pattern and lines that rhyme with nothing near them. It was built as the draft checker for a writers' room of model agents that wrote a sung duet, because language models miscount syllables. Use it to check a lyric before it is set to music or sent to a song generator, to compare the syllable counts of verses that share one melody, or as the draft_hook of an expert-panel writers' room.
scorebug: A live fantasy football dashboard that runs in a Cloudflare Worker, with a Mac app and an iPhone app (widget and Live Activity) on top. The heavy lineup model runs in Python and posts its inputs; the Worker adds ESPN's live points and the NFL game clocks and computes each matchup's win probability the same way the Python model does. It was built so the live odds work with the Mac asleep and reach the phone's lock screen, replacing a local-only page. Use it to watch a live week, to push a score or odds view to the phone, as the template for any Worker that needs live data plus a precomputed model, or as the source of per-minute win probability history for calibration work.
sdfmesh: A Python library that turns signed distance fields into closed, printable triangle meshes: it samples a field on a voxel lattice in slabs, runs marching cubes, stitches the slabs, decimates, and repairs. It also turns an image mask into a signed distance map and a local-thickness map, so a traced silhouette can become a double-sided heightfield relief joined to true 3D shapes (ellipsoids, helix tubes, rounded rings) with smooth unions. It was built to make a 3D-printable replica of a sword from a single painting, where B-rep CAD could not follow the hand-drawn vines and petals. Use it to turn a picture or logo into a keychain or relief, to sculpt organic parts such as flowers, vines or creatures in code, or to blend shapes with smooth fillets that CAD booleans make hard.
serve: Bash script that runs a Python static HTTP server on port 5031 bound to localhost for the paperclip meme generator. Written so launchd can serve the generator from ~/Documents, since bash holds the file access grant that bare Python lacks. Starting or restarting the paperclip generator; debugging why it fails under launchd; changing its port.
session-memory: CLI for MIST session memory and the vault Zettelkasten: writes session notes from transcripts, builds daily digests, backfills zettels, and indexes, lints and prunes. Built so context survives compaction and new sessions, with the model returning structured data and a script writing the files. Saving a session note; rebuilding the index; linting or pruning memory; backfilling from older sessions.
session-memory recall: Searches MIST's Zettelkasten memory in the vault and prints the best zettels for a question with their reasoned links, BM25 first and superseded notes ranked down. Built to replace raw rg over the Zettel folder, which found fewer of the notes later sessions needed in the 2026-10-15 recall eval. Use it to answer what was decided or learned about a topic, to check for an existing note before writing a new one, or to find the replacement of an outdated note.
sfx-mix: CLI that places sound effects on a timeline from a JSON cue sheet, mixes them with music, and muxes the result into a rendered video. Built to add sound design to animation renders repeatably, with synth cues and repeat options. Adding effects to an animation; checking an audio-only mix; building a new cue sheet.
shoot: Headless browser script that screenshots a scroll-story web page at every story step, each chart and the explorer, on desktop or phone viewport, with WebGL running in software so no window opens. It was built to check the Midwest AI data center atlas visually during development. Use it to review a scrollytelling page step by step, to catch label collisions or layout breaks on phones, or to grab images of a map page for a write-up.
shop: One CLI for buying anything at the lowest real price: it searches Target (RedSky, priced at the store nearest the home ZIP), Walmart (product and search JSON), Flipp weekly grocery ads, Amazon (headless Playwright) and, once keys exist, eBay's Browse API in one table, and on request Facebook Marketplace and used eBay listings around home. It also reports eBay sold prices (median, quartiles, range) through a hosted Apify actor, because every eBay-owned sold-price route is walled for personal use. Its grocery command group covers Kansas City stores without a login or a cart: a store directory with distances and closures (Price Chopper's 50 stores and operators, Cosentino's Market, Sun Fresh, Costco warehouses, Whole Foods, the walk-in independents), Whole Foods shelf prices, Costco.com online prices, the full Price Chopper and Costco weekly ads from Flipp, Cosentino's digital coupons, and the Cosentino's and Sun Fresh image-only circulars read with Apple Vision OCR. It shows one item in full, harvests and tests promo codes on a live Shopify cart without checking out, ranks offers by net cost, and hands in-store clearance lookups to Penny Lane. Use it to find the cheapest source for an exact item, search used listings near home, check what a used item actually sells for, verify whether promo codes stack, compare grocery prices and weekly ads across the stores near home, or find which store has an item on sale this week.
Site Editor: Local editor on port 5026 that makes a static site's text click-editable in place, splices edits into the source bytes, and publishes via git push. Built to edit hand-written HTML pages visually without a parser reflowing the formatting, then redeploy GitHub Pages in one step. Fixing a typo or paragraph on the personal site; publishing a small copy change without opening an editor.
Sleep Cycle Alarm: Desktop dashboard that learns Alex's average sleep-cycle length from Fitbit history and computes the best wake time for a given number of completed cycles. Made to wake at a cycle boundary in light sleep rather than mid deep sleep, using personal data instead of the generic 90-minute rule. Choosing a wake time for tonight; checking how the learned cycle length has shifted; feeding an alarm with the calculated time.
Solo DM: Launcher that starts the solo D&D web UI server on port 8765 and opens the browser for the theory-of-magic campaign. Provides a one-click entry to the automated solo D&D 5e game where Claude acts as a grounded, real-dice Dungeon Master. Resuming a solo D&D session; starting the solo campaign UI; checking the server health endpoint.
song-sync: uv script that detects a song's tempo and first beat with librosa and writes them, plus optional lyric cue times, into the animation project's config. Built so dances, pulses, and cuts in the animation kit lock to a generated song's actual timing instead of guessed values. Starting an animation or music video from a song; correcting tempo with --bpm; adding lyric timings; previewing with --dry-run.
spotify-dl: Python CLI that downloads a Spotify track by URL or ID using embed-endpoint metadata and librespot audio, avoiding the rate-limited Web API. The shared OAuth client used by zotify returns 429 almost always, so tag lookups broke downloads. It requires Premium. Downloading a track from a Spotify link; diagnosing 429 or audio-key failures; logging in with --login.
square-loyalty: Command-line reader for Square Loyalty programs on any Square Online store. It reads the program rules (earn categories, reward tiers, expiry), looks up a loyalty balance and lifetime points by phone, and with --menu ranks the store's menu by price with each item marked as earning or redeemable. Built to read Alex's punch-card balance at a local coffee shop whose rewards show only inside Cash App, which has no API. Use it to check a rewards balance at a Square shop, to find the cheapest item that still earns a point, to see what a reward can be spent on, or to compare loyalty terms across shops.
ssd-watch: Shell script that watches /Volumes through launchd and keeps the Trawl media app tied to its portable SSD. When the SSD goes from mounted to not mounted, it quits the Trawl window and stops the Trawl server job; when the SSD mounts, it starts the server. Built because Trawl started at every login even with the drive unplugged, and launchd cannot stop a job when its KeepAlive path disappears. Use it as a pattern when an app must run only while a specific drive is connected, to debug why Trawl closed or did not start, or to retarget Trawl at a different drive name.
stalled-repos: Finds public GitHub projects that other people started and abandoned before AI-assisted coding (last commit before 2022-11-30). It harvests candidates from Hacker News through the Algolia API and from GitHub search by README keywords and topics, pulls metadata and READMEs through GraphQL, removes forks, lists and recently active repos, and writes ranked batches for an agent judgment pass. It was built to look for weird ideas and dead-but-loved games worth finishing or reviving. Use it to look for abandoned projects in a new niche (change the keyword and topic lists), to find an unfinished open-source tool before you build one from scratch, or to find old game reimplementations to revive.
standings-history: Replays the fantasy league's schedule from the ESPN API and rebuilds the standings table after every decided week, ranked by win percentage then points for, the same as ESPN. It can print the history, emit JSON, or write an interactive bump chart with our team and the two nearest rivals in color and hover tracing for every other team. Built to show how the whole league's positions moved week by week. Use it for a standings-over-time chart, to find when a team crossed the bye or playoff line, as input to a weekly recap, or to check a team's record history.
standings-post: Posts the fantasy league's standings bump chart to a Discord channel once per decided week. It renders the chart from standings_history.py to a PNG with headless Playwright and uploads it with a short caption (bye seats, biggest climb and drop). It was made so the league channel gets the weekly chart with no manual step. Use it to repost a week's chart, to preview the caption with --dry-run, or as the pattern for any scheduled image post to Discord.
standings_history.py: Replays a fantasy league's ESPN schedule and rebuilds the standings table after each decided week, ranked by win percentage and then points for. It was made to show how the league table moved week by week, as an interactive bump chart with bye and playoff cut lines. Use it to draw a standings-over-time chart, to check how a team's rank changed after a given week, or to feed a weekly recap post.
stash-scan: A read-only scan of the fantasy league's injured free agents that prices each one as a playoff stash: the chance he is back (0.53, measured on past NFL seasons) times how much better than our weakest eligible starter he would score on return, summed over the per-week title weights from the season simulator. It was built when the playoff weeks were measured at about eleven times a regular-season week, because the waiver scan skipped every injured player and so could not see a star worth holding in an empty IR slot. Use it in the weekly waiver review from the middle of the season, when an IR slot opens, before dropping an injured player of our own, or to check whether a big name on the wire would actually start for us in the fantasy playoffs. With --banner it sends one Do it or Skip notification for a candidate that fits the open IR slot.
ste-check: Checks English text against the ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English Issue 9 dictionary and sentence-length limits. Built when STE became the default register for MIST's prose, so drafts get verified against the official spec instead of from memory. It parses the approved and rejected headwords and verb forms out of the extracted PDF text, flags each unapproved word with the spec's alternative, and marks sentences over 25 words (20 for procedures). Use it to check a runbook or README before it ships, to look up whether one word is approved, or to audit a document for readers who are not native English speakers.
stream-scan: Read-only Python CLI applying the playbook's kicker and defense streaming thresholds using ESPN matchup pricing, flagging bye weeks two weeks ahead. Built because a deterministic streaming rule was written into the playbook on 2026-09-11 that nothing actually ran. Running before Tuesday waiver claims; checking upcoming bye weeks; finding streaming candidates.
substack-draft: A command-line tool that reads an Obsidian note and creates a draft post on a Substack publication. It uploads embedded vault images, keeps every hyperlink, and uses the logged-in browser session for auth. It was made to move a finished essay from the vault into Substack without a copy and paste pass that lost links and images. Use it to send a new essay to Substack, to make a fresh draft after big edits to a note, or to check with --dry-run how a note converts before upload.
subtile-ocr: Command-line OCR that turns DVD bitmap subtitles (VobSub idx/sub) into SRT text with Tesseract. Installed to get the official English subtitles off a DVD ISO and move them onto a higher-resolution Blu-ray rip that had none. Use it to pull text subtitles from a DVD rip, to make bitmap subtitles editable or retimeable, or to add a soft English track to a video when the only subtitle source is a disc image.
sunday-poweron: Bash script that arms a one-off pmset power-on for the coming Sunday at 10:20 AM and is re-run by a root LaunchDaemon each Monday and at boot. Built because pmset allows only one repeating wake, so the second weekly time must be a re-armed one-off, ensuring fantasy lineup routines run even if the Mac was shut down. Checking the Sunday wake with pmset -g sched; reinstalling the daemon; adjusting the power-on time.
supernote-parser.py: Python script that extracts PNG page images from a Supernote .note file using supernotelib, for vision-based handwriting OCR. Built as the first step of the handwritten-note pipeline, turning device files into images that a vision model can read. Processing a new Supernote note; re-extracting pages from a .note file; fixing an UnsupportedFileFormat error after a firmware update.
supernote-print-job: Print command for ippeveprinter that delivers each print job PDF to the Supernote over the LAN or a cloud sync folder. Built so printing from any Mac app sends a document to the Supernote as a virtual printer. Debugging a failed print to the Supernote; changing the delivery fallback; sending a PDF for handwriting.
supernote-print-server: Bash script that runs macOS ippeveprinter as a PDF-accepting IPP printer named Supernote, handing each job to a delivery script. Built to print from any macOS dialog straight to the Supernote, inspired by firmware that speaks IPP. Starting or restarting the Supernote print queue; changing the port; diagnosing a print job that never reaches the device.
swap-scan: Read-only script that scores every bench-for-wire swap against the playbook's 20-point season gate using blended rest-of-season projections. At a full roster every claim is a swap, so value is add minus drop over the season, not the add's projection alone. Weekly waiver review; checking a bye-week hole; evaluating a claim before filing it.
switchboard-kc-smoke: A read-only health check of a deployed Switchboard KC web server against the live city API: config, key health, the catalog, my reports, a report detail, a map query, the duplicate check, and the server's guards (no session, a foreign origin, a bad id, a point outside Kansas City, a report for another city). It was made to prove the proxy works end to end after each deploy without filing anything. Use it after deploying the Switchboard KC web server, when the city may have changed its API or key, or when a user says the web app stopped loading reports.
sync-anims: Shell script that rsyncs the MIST crystal animation packs from mist-anims into the Console's gitignored static/anims folder at 96 px and 256 px. Keeps the Console's UI chrome and transcript wallpaper on the same clips as the animation project. After re-rendering crystal animations; setting up a fresh Console clone; after adding a new state or emotion.
Table Conductor: Native Mac app for running tabletop RPG audio at an in-person game, modeled on the Pocket Bard app: scenes with explore, combat and victory music, an intensity slider, layered ambience with I/II/III levels, one-shot sound effects, and previews in a Manage sheet. The app window is the stage that plays the audio; phones on the same network open the same page as a remote. It was made to replace a Pocket Bard subscription with open and free music, ambience and sound effects. Use it to run music and ambience during a session, to build scenes for a campaign location, or to add Tabletop Audio, Freesound or YouTube Music cues to a scene.
talify.py: Python discovery lane that queries Missouri's Talify job board JSON endpoint in a remote pass and a Kansas City local pass, then verifies pay from each job's detail page. Added as a state-government job source for /job-search; the board's server ignores a maximum-compensation filter, so the script enforces the pay band client-side. Job discovery sweeps for Missouri state and local government roles; checking recent postings with a days window; re-verifying compensation before recommending a listing.
testflight-feedback: A command that reads TestFlight beta feedback from the App Store Connect API: screenshot reports with their comments, crash reports with the full crash log, and the recent builds with their processing state. It was made because TestFlight feedback is only visible in the App Store Connect website, and a report sent from the phone could not reach MIST. Use it when Alex says he reported a bug or crash in a TestFlight app, to check that an uploaded build finished processing, or to collect all feedback on an app since a date before a fix pass.
testflight-fleet: A command-line batch that ships every iOS app listed in bin/testflight-apps.json to TestFlight. For each app it checks App Store Connect for a record, then archives and uploads it one at a time, and names the apps that still need a record. It was made to move all of the apps on the phone to TestFlight at once, after the list of apps that were said to be on TestFlight turned out to have no records. Use it to release every app after a shared change, to check which apps have a record (--check), or to ship a subset (--only).
testflight-ready: A command-line step that runs after a TestFlight upload. It waits for App Store Connect to finish processing the build, makes sure the app has an internal tester group that receives every build, adds the testers from the other apps' internal groups, and sends a banner and a Discord DM when an invite still needs a tap. It was made because a new app record had no tester group, so an uploaded build never appeared in the TestFlight app on the phone. Use it after any iOS upload, to check why a build does not show in TestFlight, or to set up testers for a new app.
testflight-upload: A command that archives an XcodeGen iOS project in Release and uploads it to TestFlight, with a timestamp build number and a check that every target in the archive carries that number. It was made to move several personal iPhone apps from direct Xcode installs to TestFlight with one shared path, in place of a copied upload script in each repo. Use it to ship a new build of any app that is already on TestFlight, to put a new app on TestFlight (run --archive-only first so the bundle ids register, then make the App Store Connect record), or to check that an app still builds in Release.
The Great Wheel Editor: A double-click launcher for the local editor of The Great Wheel, a public 3D map of the D&D multiverse. It starts the local editor server (which first pulls the latest changes from GitHub) and opens the map in edit mode, or reopens the server that already runs. It was built so the map can be edited and published without a terminal, because the published website has no edit mode. Use it to add or change spheres, currents and bodies, to write DM notes, and to publish.
The Priory: Native app shell around a self-hosted news aggregator with bias bars, factuality ratings, blindspot detection, and prediction-market charts on stories. Built to update priors on the news with a deterministic-first pipeline, forked from an open-source aggregator, replacing manual outlet comparison. Reading the news with bias context; finding blindspot stories; checking market odds tied to a story.
Tiny Tools: App launcher for a local web server on port 5007 hosting a set of small utilities, keeping the Dock icon alive while the server runs. Built so small single-purpose tools (with uv and rembg available on PATH) are one click away. Quick image tasks such as background removal; opening the utilities page; quitting to stop the server.
tools-registry-scan.py: Scans app launchers, launchd jobs, bin/ executables and hand-logged tools, then rewrites the Obsidian Tools notes that the registry bases render. Built so there is one auto-discovered source of truth for what has been built, and previously automated work does not get redone by hand. Rebuilding the registry after adding a tool or job; checking why a tool is missing from Tools.base; verifying live port and job status.
traces: Command-line tool that keeps a zstd archive of every Claude Code session transcript on the Mac, loads it into a DuckDB trace table with sessions, API calls, tool calls, prompts and system events, computes window metrics and saved baselines, and serves a local page for labeling a fixed sample of sessions pass or fail. It was built because Claude Code deletes transcripts after its cleanup period and the backup skipped them, which left only the assistant's own summaries of past sessions as a record. Use it to measure a harness change against a saved baseline, to find the tools or skills with the most errors, to run an error-analysis labeling round on real traces, or to pull real tasks for an eval set.
Trawl: Local media search and torrent app on port 5021 that searches several indexers at once, hands results to an rqbit engine, and enforces Mullvad VPN use. Built to make finding and downloading media one step while guaranteeing no torrent traffic leaves outside the VPN tunnel. Searching for a movie, show or file; subscribing to a series for automatic episodes; checking download progress with the VPN on.
trip: A command-line pipeline that turns a trip.json into a shareable backpacking plan. It routes each day on OpenStreetMap trail data, samples USGS 3DEP elevations, pulls USFS land ownership and USGS NHD creeks, checks that every camp sits on Forest Service land, writes GPX files, uploads the route to AllTrails, and publishes an interactive Leaflet map page as an unlisted page on the personal site. It was built on 2026-10-06 to make the Cedar Creek trip plans repeatable instead of a pile of one-off scripts. Use it to plan a new overnight or multi-day hike, to check whether a planned campsite is on public land, to measure daily miles and elevation gain for a route, or to send a group one link with the map, days and conditions.
tta-sync: Mirrors the Tabletop Audio 10-minute ambience tracks to a local folder and writes a JSON manifest with each track's title, file URL, mood, action, setting and biome tags, and keywords. It reads the same data scripts the tabletopaudio.com page loads, so it picks up new tracks without a third-party list. It was made for the table-conductor RPG audio player, which replaced the out-of-date community YAML mirror of the track list. Use it to refresh the ambience library, to find ambience tracks by mood or scene type, or as a template for scraping the track lists of a site that keeps its catalog in front-end JavaScript.
Turn To: Native Mac window for the Turn To gamebook reader, an app-shell wrapper around the local server on port 5034. It was built so a Fighting Fantasy gamebook can be played on its own scanned pages, with the printed Adventure Sheet, photoreal dice, fights and saves, without a browser tab. Open it to play a gamebook, continue a saved adventure, or check a book file after rebuilding it.
Turn To book pipeline: A set of scripts that turns a scanned gamebook into a book file for the Turn To reader: section text, choices, enemy stat blocks, the position of every 'turn to' link on each page image, and the rules each section asks for. It was built to make a Fighting Fantasy gamebook playable on its own scanned pages, merging two scans so each catches the other's OCR errors. Use it to add another numbered-section gamebook, to rebuild a book after fixing its text, or to check that every section of a gamebook can be reached.
turn-to: Command that makes sure the Turn To server is up and opens the reader in the browser. It was added so the gamebook reader starts with one command from a terminal, the same way on any Mac with the repository. Use it to open the reader, to start the server for the app window, or with --serve before testing the app headless.
turn-to-server: Small Python web server that sends only the Turn To app and the built book folders, never the scans, OCR output or notes beside them. It replaced a plain directory server, which exposed the source PDFs. Use it to serve the reader locally, with --lan to read on a phone on the same Wi-Fi, or as the launchd job behind the app window.
tv: Python CLI for the second-floor Samsung TV over its local secure WebSocket: power, volume, key codes, app launch, status and a full-screen TUI console. Built to control the TV from the terminal and from MIST instead of the remote. Turning the TV on or off; launching Netflix, Plex or another app; sending volume or key commands; checking TV status in a script.
tv-agent: Command-line client for the MIST TV Agent, a sideloaded service on the Samsung TV that installs, removes and launches apps through the TV's own developer bridge and edits TizenBrew's module config. It was built because every app update needed the TV's Host PC IP switched between the Mac and the TV's loopback address, each switch costing a store-API window and a restart. Use it to push a rebuilt tile or module package, read the Smart Hub app list, launch an app on the TV, change which module the Criterion tile opens, or run a restricted bridge command.
twocam-diarize: Writes who-spoke-when JSON for a video or audio file with pyannote speaker diarization, giving the audio to the model in memory so a broken torchcodec install does not matter. Built as the speaker source for twocam-stitch. Use it to split any recording by speaker, count talk time per person, or find the longest turn of each voice for a transcript spot check.
twocam-stitch: Cuts two camera angles of one recorded conversation into a single video that always shows the person who is talking. It syncs the files by audio cross-correlation, cuts on diarized speaker turns (or on the level difference between the two mics), keeps the cleaner audio track, and renders 4K HEVC in one ffmpeg pass. Built to stitch two-GoPro street conversations at an outreach table, replacing a manual multicam edit. Use it for interviews, podcasts filmed on two phones or cameras, matching which files from two cameras belong together (the pair mode), or finding the sync offset between any two recordings of the same audio.
unmix: A command-line pipeline that makes an instrumental and an a cappella of a real song. It downloads the best audio stream from the user's own YouTube Music Premium account through browser cookies, separates it with RoFormer models through python-audio-separator, checks the result with Whisper lyric recall and a Demucs second opinion, and exports a tagged 24-bit FLAC and a 320k MP3 with cover art. It was built for a request to remove the vocals from a classic rock track in high quality, and it replaced a one-off chain of yt-dlp, separator and ffmpeg commands. Use it to make a karaoke or practice track, to isolate a vocal for a remix or transcription, to compare separation models or ensembles on one song, or to download a track from YouTube Music at the best quality the account gets.
ups-track: Command-line tool and MCP server that reads UPS package status and the full scan history from the public tracking page through an off-screen real Chrome. Built because the official UPS API needs a shipper account and ups.com blocks curl and every headless browser. Use it to check where a return or a delivery is, to confirm that a retailer received a package, or to give a chat a track_package tool for UPS numbers.
vendor: Shell script that copies pinned front-end libraries (map, chart, scroll animation) and self-hosted fonts from node_modules into a static site folder, converts Census state outlines to GeoJSON, and records the versions. It was built so the Midwest AI data center atlas loads every file from its own GitHub Pages origin with no CDN. Use it after updating a library in that atlas, or as a pattern for vendoring npm packages into a no-build static site.
vendor-sync.sh: Shell script that refreshes the vendored UI libraries (Beer CSS, mdui, material-color-utilities, Material Symbols) to the versions pinned in vendor.json. Built so new apps can pull a known, pinned set of Material Design libraries from one local repo instead of fetching each separately. After bumping a version in vendor.json; setting up the material-design repo on a new machine; before starting a new UI project.
vendor.mjs: Copies the Switchboard KC web app's third-party files (Beer CSS, MapLibre GL JS) from node_modules into the served folder, strips the Beer CSS font rules that would load from a CDN, and builds a Material Symbols font with only the icons the app uses. It was made so the web app serves every library from its own origin under a strict Content-Security-Policy, with an icon font about one twentieth of the full size. Use it after adding an icon or updating a library in the Switchboard KC web app, or as a pattern for subsetting Material Symbols in another no-build web project.
verify-quotes: A quote checker for Markdown notes. It reads the quote callouts in a note and searches a folder of source text (book chapters, episode transcripts) for each one, then reports where each quote occurs with the text around it, or reports it as missing. It was made for the council skill, to prove that every quote in a council member note is the exact words of the character in canon, because many popular quotes online are fan-made. Use it to fact-check quotes in any note before it ships, to find which chapter or episode a remembered line comes from, to catch misattributed quotes in a draft, or to check a new council member note against its corpus.
Video Downloader: Small local macOS app on port 5005 wrapping a Flask server and yt-dlp, with a static embed resolver and browser sniff fallback. Built as a simple double-click way to save video or audio from the web, including sites yt-dlp cannot extract alone. Saving a video or audio file from a URL; handling a site where yt-dlp fails; grabbing a clip for offline use.
volume: Python CLI that pulls nflverse weekly stats and snap counts, joins them to ESPN rosters, and flags BUY, SELL, ROLE-UP, and ROLE-DOWN based on volume versus points rank. Nothing in season measured volume, though the playbook's edge rests on it, so this supplies opportunity metrics. Weekly waiver and trade decisions; ranking free agents by position volume; refreshing the player variance cache used by lineup checks.
wait-for-network.sh: Bash script that blocks until the network and DNS work, or gives up after a bounded wait, meant to prefix launchd commands. Created after wake-time launchd jobs began failing with ENOTFOUND because Wi-Fi and DNS were not yet ready, with no retry until the next day. Gating any launchd job that calls the network; fixing a job that fails only right after wake; chaining before an API-calling script.
wake-watch: Reads the next seven days of the primary Google Calendar and compares each morning's first real commitment with the end of the recurring Sleep block. When the event start, minus the morning routine and any travel, falls before that wake time, it sets a one-time iPhone alarm through the MIST Alarms hub, and it moves or removes that alarm when the event changes. It was made so that early meetings do not depend on Alex noticing them the night before. Use it to check which mornings need an early alarm, to preview the plan with --dry-run, or as the model for other calendar-driven phone alarms.
where: CLI that turns a day of GPS points into stays, moves and no-data gaps, then names each stay from Home, a hand-kept places file, or a cached OpenStreetMap reverse geocode. Built so the evening wind-down can say where Alex went and which planned calendar entries had no matching visit, because Google Maps Timeline has no API. Also imports a Google Timeline export for history. Use it to recap where someone was on a date, to check a calendar entry against a real visit, to backfill old days from a Timeline export, or to find unplanned long stops.
workday.py: Python lane that polls the unauthenticated Workday CXS search endpoint for each saved tenant board, diffs against a snapshot, and gates results mechanically on location, time type, and compensation. Built because many mid-market and enterprise employers post only on Workday and never crosspost, so search engines miss them; sibling of the Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby watcher. Scheduled or manual polling of employers known to use Workday; pinning a recruiter-shared filtered board URL with --add; catching new postings since the last snapshot.
yt-transcript: Fetches YouTube captions through yt-dlp and cleans them into readable text, preferring human subtitles and removing karaoke tags and repeated rolling-window lines. Raw auto-captions carry inline timing tags and repeat every line, roughly doubling tokens and reading like a stutter, so a bare yt-dlp dump is poor model input. Summarizing or quoting a YouTube video; getting timestamped captions; listing available caption languages; saving a transcript to a note.
zettel_maintain.py: Weekly upkeep pass for MIST's Zettelkasten: links orphan notes, merges near-duplicates, closes stale open threads only with evidence, merges synonym tags, writes structure hub notes and records health metrics. Built from primary Zettelkasten and agent-memory sources when the store outgrew per-session writing. Use it to clean up the memory store after a burst of sessions, rebuild topic hubs, or measure store health.
zulip-admin: Stdlib Python admin CLI for the friends' Zulip org covering users, bots, streams, invites, bot minting and ownership transfer, and MIST usage reports. Built to run the friends' Claude chat org from the terminal, with each command printing the API result so failures are visible. Inviting a friend; minting a bot for someone; reconciling bot owners; checking who used MIST and the cost.
